rules.legal_concept: Right of inspection by any requester
rules.atomic_rule: Any requester (any person requesting inspection or copies of a record) has a right to inspect any record, except as otherwise provided by law.
rules.trigger: A record request is received
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, any requester has a right to inspect any record. ... 'Requester' means any person who requests inspection or copies of a record, except a committed or incarcerated person, unless the person requests inspection or copies of a record that contains specific references to that person or his or her minor children ...
rules.notes: Universal-access rule; the statute grants the right to 'any' requester with no class limitation except the committed/incarcerated carve-out captured in WI-0005.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A request may not be refused because the requester is unwilling to state the purpose of the request.
rules.trigger: Requester declines to state purpose
rules.source_language: Except as authorized under this paragraph, no request under pars. (a) and (b) to (f) may be refused because the person making the request is unwilling to be identified or to state the purpose of the request.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key.

rules.legal_concept: Requester need not be identified
rules.atomic_rule: A request may not be refused because the requester is unwilling to be identified, except where acceptable identification may be required for records kept at a private residence or where security/federal law requires.
rules.trigger: Requester declines to identify self
rules.source_language: Except as authorized under this paragraph, no request ... may be refused because the person making the request is unwilling to be identified or to state the purpose of the request. ... A requester may be required to show acceptable identification whenever the requested record is kept at a private residence or whenever security reasons or federal law or regulations so require.
rules.notes: Anonymity is the default; conditional ID exception is captured separately in WI-0013.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: No residency or citizenship qualification is imposed on a requester; any requester has the right to inspect any record.
rules.trigger: Request received from a non-resident
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, any requester has a right to inspect any record. ... it is declared to be the public policy of this state that all persons are entitled to the greatest possible information regarding the affairs of government ...
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule per universal-access symmetry. 'No residency requirement' is inferred from the 'any requester'/'all persons' language; Wisconsin imposes no residency limitation in ch. 19 subch. II.

rules.legal_concept: Committed/incarcerated person excluded from 'requester'
rules.atomic_rule: A committed or incarcerated person is not a 'requester' with general access rights unless the requested record contains specific references to that person or his or her minor children (for whom physical placement has not been denied) and the record is otherwise accessible to the person by law.
rules.trigger: Requester is a committed or incarcerated person
rules.source_language: 'Requester' means any person who requests inspection or copies of a record, except a committed or incarcerated person, unless the person requests inspection or copies of a record that contains specific references to that person or his or her minor children for whom he or she has not been denied physical placement under ch. 767, and the record is otherwise accessible to the person by law.
rules.notes: Definitions of 'committed person' (19.32(1b)) and 'incarcerated person' (19.32(1c)) govern this classification.

rules.legal_concept: Enhanced right to own personally identifiable information
rules.atomic_rule: A requester who is the individual (or person authorized by the individual) has an additional right to inspect and copy personally identifiable information pertaining to that individual, subject to the enumerated exceptions (enforcement/investigation records, life/safety, informant, security, etc.).
rules.trigger: Requester seeks PII pertaining to self and identifies self
rules.source_language: In addition to any right under par. (a), any requester who is an individual or person authorized by the individual has a right to inspect any personally identifiable information pertaining to the individual in a record ... maintained by an authority and to make or receive a copy of any such information. The right to inspect or copy information in a record under this paragraph does not apply to any of the following ...
rules.notes: Not subject to the public-interest balancing test (Hempel v. City of Baraboo, 2005 WI 120). Triggers the 19.35(4)(c) determination sequence (WI-0067).

rules.legal_concept: 'Authority' having custody of a record
rules.atomic_rule: An 'authority' subject to the law is any listed governmental body or officer having custody of a record, including a state or local office, elective official, agency, board, committee, special purpose district, court, and certain publicly funded nonprofits; the request must be directed to the authority with custody.
rules.trigger: Determining whether the recipient of a request is a covered authority
rules.source_language: 'Authority' means any of the following having custody of a record: a state or local office, elective official, agency, board, commission, committee, council, department or public body corporate and politic created by the constitution or by any law, ordinance, rule or order; ... a special purpose district; any court of law; ... a nonprofit corporation which receives more than 50 percent of its funds from a county or a municipality ... or a formally constituted subunit of any of the foregoing.
rules.notes: Only the authority (e.g., the municipality itself) is the proper recipient; an independent-contractor assessor was not an 'authority' (WIREdata v. Village of Sussex, 2008 WI 69).

rules.legal_concept: 'Record' and its exclusions
rules.atomic_rule: A 'record' is any recorded information created or kept by an authority regardless of form, but excludes drafts/notes/preliminary materials prepared for the originator's personal use, purely personal materials, copyright/patent/bequest-limited materials, and published materials available for sale or at a public library.
rules.trigger: Determining whether the requested item is a 'record'
rules.source_language: 'Record' means any material on which written, drawn, printed, spoken, visual, or electromagnetic information or electronically generated or stored data is recorded or preserved ... that has been created or is being kept by an authority. ... 'Record' does not include drafts, notes, preliminary computations, and like materials prepared for the originator's personal use ...; materials that are purely the personal property of the custodian ...; materials to which access is limited by copyright, patent, or bequest; and published materials ... available for sale, or that are available for inspection at a public library.
rules.notes: 'Record' does not include identical copies of otherwise available records (Stone v. Board of Regents, 2007 WI App 223).

rules.legal_concept: Oral requests allowed
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be made orally, but must be reduced to writing before an enforcement action under s. 19.37 is commenced.
rules.trigger: Requester submits an oral request
rules.source_language: A request may be made orally, but a request must be in writing before an action to enforce the request is commenced under s. 19.37.
rules.notes: Writing is a prerequisite only for enforcement (see WI-0064), not for making the request.

rules.legal_concept: Mailed requests allowed
rules.atomic_rule: A request may not be refused because it is received by mail, unless prepayment of a fee is required under s. 19.35(3)(f).
rules.trigger: Request received by mail
rules.source_language: Except as authorized under this paragraph, no request under pars. (a) to (f) may be refused because the request is received by mail, unless prepayment of a fee is required under sub. (3) (f).
rules.notes: A $1.29 prepayment demand for a mail request was not permitted (Borzych v. Paluszcyk, 201 Wis. 2d 523) because it did not exceed the $5 threshold.

rules.legal_concept: Sufficiency of a request
rules.atomic_rule: A request is deemed sufficient if it reasonably describes the requested record or information requested.
rules.trigger: Evaluating whether a request is actionable
rules.source_language: A request under pars. (a) to (f) is deemed sufficient if it reasonably describes the requested record or the information requested.
rules.notes: 'Reasonably describes' is a soft standard the engine applies, not a numeric value.

rules.legal_concept: Request lacking reasonable limitation
rules.atomic_rule: A request for a record without a reasonable limitation as to subject matter or length of time represented by the record does not constitute a sufficient request and may be rejected.
rules.trigger: Request lacks reasonable subject-matter or time limitation
rules.source_language: However, a request for a record without a reasonable limitation as to subject matter or length of time represented by the record does not constitute a sufficient request.
rules.notes: Volume alone is not sufficient reason to reject; the custodian need not take affirmative steps to narrow (Gehl v. Connors, 2007 WI App 238; Schopper v. Gehring, 210 Wis. 2d 208).

rules.legal_concept: Acceptable identification in limited circumstances
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may be required to show acceptable identification whenever the requested record is kept at a private residence, or whenever security reasons or federal law/regulations so require.
rules.trigger: Record kept at private residence, or security/federal-law conditions apply
rules.source_language: A requester may be required to show acceptable identification whenever the requested record is kept at a private residence or whenever security reasons or federal law or regulations so require.
rules.notes: Narrow exception to the default anonymity rule (WI-0003).

rules.legal_concept: Posted procedural-information notice
rules.atomic_rule: Each authority shall adopt, prominently display, and make available a notice describing its organization, the times/places and legal custodian from whom, and methods whereby, the public may obtain access to and copies of records, and the costs thereof; the notice shall separately identify each local/state public office position.
rules.trigger: Authority is subject to the public records law
rules.source_language: Each authority shall adopt, prominently display and make available for inspection and copying at its offices, for the guidance of the public, a notice containing a description of its organization and the established times and places at which, the legal custodian under s. 19.33 from whom, and the methods whereby, the public may obtain information and access to records in its custody, make requests for records, or obtain copies of records, and the costs thereof.
rules.notes: Does not apply to members of the legislature or of any local governmental body.

rules.legal_concept: Written designation of legal custodian
rules.atomic_rule: Every authority not otherwise specified shall designate in writing one or more positions as legal custodian to fulfill the authority's duties under the subchapter, vested with full legal power to render decisions and carry out those duties.
rules.trigger: Authority must be able to respond to requests
rules.source_language: Every authority not specified in subs. (1) to (3) shall designate in writing one or more positions occupied by an officer or employee of the authority or the unit of government of which it is a part as a legal custodian to fulfill its duties under this subchapter. ... The legal custodian shall be vested by the authority with full legal power to render decisions and carry out the duties of the authority under this subchapter.
rules.notes: An elective official is the legal custodian of his or her own records (19.33(1)) but may designate a staff employee.

rules.legal_concept: Default legal custodian absent designation
rules.atomic_rule: In the absence of a designation, the authority's highest ranking officer and the chief administrative officer (if any) are the legal custodians.
rules.trigger: No legal custodian has been designated
rules.source_language: In the absence of a designation the authority's highest ranking officer and the chief administrative officer, if any, are the legal custodians for the authority.

rules.legal_concept: Deputy legal custodian for absences
rules.atomic_rule: The legal custodian (or appointing authority) of records in a publicly owned/leased building shall designate one or more deputies to act as legal custodian in his or her absence or as otherwise required to respond to requests under s. 19.35(4).
rules.trigger: Legal custodian is absent
rules.source_language: The legal custodian of records maintained in a publicly owned or leased building or the authority appointing the legal custodian shall designate one or more deputies to act as legal custodian of such records in his or her absence or as otherwise required to respond to requests as provided in s. 19.35 (4).
rules.notes: Does not apply to members of the legislature or any local governmental body.

rules.legal_concept: Local IT authority is not custodian of law enforcement records
rules.atomic_rule: A local information technology authority holding a law enforcement record only for storage/processing is not the legal custodian; the custodian is the authority for which the record is stored, and the IT authority shall deny any portion of a request relating to a local law enforcement record.
rules.trigger: Request directed to a local IT authority storing law enforcement records
rules.source_language: For purposes of requests for access to records under sub. (1), a local information technology authority that has custody of a law enforcement record for the primary purpose of information storage, information technology processing, or other information technology usage is not the legal custodian of the record. ... A local information technology authority that receives a request under sub. (1) for access to information in a law enforcement record shall deny any portion of the request that relates to information in a local law enforcement record.
rules.notes: Routing rule: request must be redirected to the owning law-enforcement authority.

rules.legal_concept: Access during regular office hours
rules.atomic_rule: An authority that maintains regular office hours at the location where records are kept shall permit access to those records at all times during those office hours, unless otherwise specifically authorized by law.
rules.trigger: Authority maintains regular office hours at the records location
rules.source_language: Each authority which maintains regular office hours at the location where records in the custody of the authority are kept shall permit access to the records of the authority at all times during those office hours, unless otherwise specifically authorized by law.

rules.legal_concept: 48-hour access notice where no regular hours
rules.clock_spec: floor: 48 hours advance written or oral notice of intent to inspect/copy
rules.atomic_rule: An authority without regular office hours at the records location may require at least 48 hours' written or oral notice of intent to inspect or copy before permitting access.
rules.trigger: Authority does not maintain regular office hours at records location
rules.source_language: Each authority which does not maintain regular office hours at the location where records in the custody of the authority are kept shall: 1. Permit access to its records upon at least 48 hours' written or oral notice of intent to inspect or copy a record ...
rules.notes: Alternative to the weekly access window in WI-0021; the 48-hour figure is a statutory floor ('at least').

rules.legal_concept: Weekly 2-hour access window alternative
rules.clock_spec: floor: 2 consecutive hours per week access window; may require 24 hours advance notice
rules.atomic_rule: As an alternative, such an authority may establish a period of at least 2 consecutive hours per week during which access is permitted, and may then require 24 hours' advance written or oral notice of intent to inspect or copy.
rules.trigger: Authority elects the weekly-window option
rules.source_language: 2. Establish a period of at least 2 consecutive hours per week during which access to the records of the authority is permitted. In such case, the authority may require 24 hours' advance written or oral notice of intent to inspect or copy a record.
rules.notes: The 2-hour/week and 24-hour figures are statutory floors.

rules.legal_concept: Comparable inspection/copying facilities
rules.atomic_rule: The authority shall provide facilities comparable to those used by its employees to inspect, copy, and abstract the record during established office hours, but is not required to purchase/lease equipment or provide a separate room.
rules.trigger: Requester is authorized to inspect or copy a record
rules.source_language: The authority shall provide any person who is authorized to inspect or copy a record under sub. (1) (a), (am), (b) or (f) with facilities comparable to those used by its employees to inspect, copy and abstract the record during established office hours. An authority is not required by this subsection to purchase or lease photocopying, duplicating, photographic or other equipment or to provide a separate room ...

rules.legal_concept: Time for compliance — as soon as practicable and without delay
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as practicable and without delay" from request receipt
rules.atomic_rule: Upon any request, the authority shall, as soon as practicable and without delay, either fill the request or notify the requester of its determination to deny the request in whole or in part and the reasons therefor.
rules.trigger: Any record request is received
rules.source_language: Each authority, upon request for any record, shall, as soon as practicable and without delay, either fill the request or notify the requester of the authority's determination to deny the request in whole or in part and the reasons therefor.
rules.notes: Soft/undefined standard — no numeric day-count. 'Reasonable time' depends on the nature, staff/resources, and extent of the request (WIREdata v. Village of Sussex, 2008 WI 69). Sub. (4)(a) does not require immediate disclosure (Journal Times, 2015 WI 56).

rules.legal_concept: Exclusion of weekends and holidays from time periods
rules.atomic_rule: When a time period (in hours or days) is provided for performing an act under ss. 19.33 to 19.39, the whole of Saturday, Sunday, and any legal holiday (midnight to midnight) is excluded in computing the period.
rules.trigger: Any statutory time period is being computed
rules.source_language: In ss. 19.33 to 19.39, when a time period is provided for performing an act, whether the period is expressed in hours or days, the whole of Saturday, Sunday, and any legal holiday, from midnight to midnight, shall be excluded in computing the period.
rules.notes: Governs computation of every hour/day clock in the subchapter (e.g., the 5-day, 60-day, 3/5/10/12-day periods).

rules.legal_concept: Indefinite future-date response is a denial
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian is not authorized to comply with a request at some unspecified future date; such a response constitutes a denial of the request.
rules.trigger: Authority responds that it will comply at an unspecified future date
rules.clock_spec: terminal: constructive denial upon indefinite-future response
rules.source_language: The custodian is not authorized to comply with an open records request at some unspecified date in the future. Such a response constitutes a denial of the request.
rules.source_authority: WTMJ, Inc. v. Sullivan, 204 Wis. 2d 452, 555 N.W.2d 125 (Ct. App. 1996)
rules.notes: Constructive-denial trigger (keeper sliver). Classifies an indefinite-delay response as a denial, opening the enforcement path.

rules.legal_concept: Written statement of reasons for denial
rules.atomic_rule: If an authority denies a written request in whole or in part, the requester shall receive from the authority a written statement of the reasons for denying the written request.
rules.trigger: A written request is denied in whole or in part
rules.source_language: If an authority denies a written request in whole or in part, the requester shall receive from the authority a written statement of the reasons for denying the written request.

rules.legal_concept: Written statement following oral denial
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from oral denial (requester's demand window)
rules.atomic_rule: If a request was made orally, the authority may deny it orally unless the requester demands a written statement of the reasons for denial within 5 business days of the oral denial.
rules.trigger: Oral request denied orally; requester demands written reasons
rules.source_language: If a request is made orally, the authority may deny the request orally unless a demand for a written statement of the reasons denying the request is made by the requester within 5 business days of the oral denial.
rules.notes: Business-day counting governed by 19.345 (WI-0024).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of review rights in written denial
rules.atomic_rule: Every written denial shall inform the requester that, if the request was made in writing, the determination is subject to review by mandamus under s. 19.37(1) or upon application to the attorney general or a district attorney.
rules.trigger: Authority issues a written denial
rules.source_language: Every written denial of a request by an authority shall inform the requester that if the request for the record was made in writing, then the determination is subject to review by mandamus under s. 19.37 (1) or upon application to the attorney general or a district attorney.
rules.notes: Required content of the denial notice pointing to the two review paths (WI-0062, WI-0063).

rules.legal_concept: Specific demonstration to deny based on open-meetings exemptions
rules.atomic_rule: The open-session (open-meetings) exemptions may be used as grounds for denying access only if the authority or legal custodian makes a specific demonstration that there is a need to restrict public access at the time the request is made.
rules.trigger: Authority relies on an open-meetings/closed-session ground to deny
rules.source_language: The exemptions to the requirement of a governmental body to meet in open session under s. 19.85 are indicative of public policy, but may be used as grounds for denying public access to a record only if the authority or legal custodian under s. 19.33 makes a specific demonstration that there is a need to restrict public access at the time that the request to inspect or copy the record is made.
rules.notes: Reflects the case-by-case public-interest balancing test; requires a contemporaneous, specific statement of public-policy reasons for denial.

rules.legal_concept: Separation of disclosable from non-disclosable information
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both disclosable and non-disclosable information, the authority shall provide the disclosable information and delete the non-disclosable information from the record before release.
rules.trigger: Record contains a mix of disclosable and exempt information
rules.source_language: If a record contains information that is subject to disclosure under s. 19.35 (1) (a) or (am) and information that is not subject to such disclosure, the authority having custody of the record shall provide the information that is subject to disclosure and delete the information that is not subject to disclosure from the record before release.
rules.notes: Separation (redaction) costs must be borne by the agency (72 Atty. Gen. 99); see fee rule WI-0033.

rules.legal_concept: Deletion/withholding to protect informant identity
rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement authority receiving a request for a record containing information (name, address, phone, voice recording, handwriting sample) that would identify an informant shall delete that portion, or withhold the record if it cannot be segregated, unless the legal custodian determines at the time of the request that the public interest in access outweighs the harm.
rules.trigger: Requested record would identify a law enforcement informant
rules.source_language: If an authority that is a law enforcement agency receives a request to inspect or copy a record or portion of a record under s. 19.35 (1) (a) that contains specific information including but not limited to a name, address, telephone number, voice recording or handwriting sample which, if disclosed, would identify an informant, the authority shall delete the portion of the record in which the information is contained or, if no portion of the record can be inspected or copied without identifying the informant, shall withhold the record unless the legal custodian ... makes a determination, at the time that the request is made, that the public interest in allowing a person to inspect, copy or receive a copy of such identifying information outweighs the harm done to the public interest by providing such access.

rules.legal_concept: Transcript where handwriting/voice would identify informant
rules.atomic_rule: If a handwritten record or voice recording must be withheld/redacted under s. 19.36(8)(b) because the handwriting or voice would identify an informant, the authority shall provide the requester, upon request, a transcript of the record or information, if otherwise subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: Handwriting/voice would identify an informant and requester asks for a transcript
rules.source_language: If an authority receives a request to inspect or copy a record that is in handwritten form or a record that is in the form of a voice recording which the authority is required to withhold or from which the authority is required to delete information under s. 19.36 (8) (b) because the handwriting or the recorded voice would identify an informant, the authority shall provide to the requester, upon his or her request, a transcript of the record or the information contained in the record if the record or information is otherwise subject to public inspection and copying under this subsection.

rules.legal_concept: No fee for redaction (general rule)
rules.clock_spec: fixed: $0 for redaction/separation of information (general records)
rules.atomic_rule: Redaction is not one of the four statutory fee tasks (reproduction/transcription, photographing/processing, locating, mailing/shipping); an authority generally may not impose a fee for the process of redacting information from a record.
rules.trigger: Authority redacts information before release
rules.source_language: Under sub. (3) the legislature provided four tasks for which an authority may impose fees on a requester: 'reproduction and transcription,' 'photographing and photographic processing,' 'locating,' and 'mailing or shipping.' ... The process of redacting information from a record does not fit into any of the four statutory tasks.
rules.source_authority: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel v. City of Milwaukee, 2012 WI 65, 341 Wis. 2d 607
rules.notes: Partially superseded for law-enforcement audio/video by 2023 Wis. Act 253 (WI-0041), which authorizes a redaction fee in that narrow context.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory withholding of financial identifying information
rules.atomic_rule: An authority shall not provide access to personally identifiable information containing an individual's account/customer number with a financial institution (including credit card, debit card, checking, or draft account numbers) unless specifically required by law.
rules.trigger: Record contains financial account/customer numbers
rules.source_language: An authority shall not provide access to personally identifiable information that contains an individual's account or customer number with a financial institution, as defined in s. 134.97 (1) (b), including credit card numbers, debit card numbers, checking account numbers, or draft account numbers, unless specifically required by law.
rules.notes: One of several mandatory-redaction categories; home address/email/phone/SSN of employees (19.36(10)) and of local/state public office holders (19.36(11)) are analogous mandatory-withholding categories noted in the coverage matrix.

rules.legal_concept: Copy/reproduction and transcription fee
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription
rules.atomic_rule: An authority may impose a fee for a copy of a record not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized by law.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for a copy of a record
rules.source_language: An authority may impose a fee upon the requester of a copy of a record which may not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription of the record, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized to be established by law.
rules.notes: No statewide fixed per-page rate; ceiling is 'actual, necessary and direct cost.' A custodian may not charge more than the actual and direct cost of reproduction (72 Atty. Gen. 36). Sub. (3)(a) defers to other statutes that specifically authorize different fees.

rules.legal_concept: Photographing fee for non-copyable records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of photographing and photographic processing
rules.atomic_rule: Where an authority provides a photograph of a record whose form does not permit copying, it may impose a fee not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of photographing and photographic processing.
rules.trigger: Authority provides a photograph of a non-copyable record
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or as authorized to be prescribed by law an authority may impose a fee upon the requester of a copy of a record that does not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of photographing and photographic processing if the authority provides a photograph of a record, the form of which does not permit copying.

rules.legal_concept: Location fee (only if $50 or more)
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of location; chargeable only if cost is $50 or more
rules.atomic_rule: An authority may impose a fee for locating a record, not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of location, but only if that cost is $50 or more.
rules.trigger: Locating the requested record costs $50 or more
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law or as authorized to be prescribed by law, an authority may impose a fee upon a requester for locating a record, not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of location, if the cost is $50 or more.
rules.notes: $50 is a chargeability threshold (no location fee below $50); the fee itself is capped at actual/necessary/direct cost. Location costs under $50 may not be added to reproduction costs to circumvent the limit. Location staff-time rate should be based on the lowest-paid employee capable of the task (DOJ guidance).

rules.legal_concept: Mailing/shipping fee
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of mailing or shipping
rules.atomic_rule: An authority may impose a fee for the actual, necessary and direct cost of mailing or shipping any copy or photograph of a record that is mailed or shipped to the requester.
rules.trigger: A copy or photograph is mailed or shipped to the requester
rules.source_language: An authority may impose a fee upon a requester for the actual, necessary and direct cost of mailing or shipping of any copy or photograph of a record which is mailed or shipped to the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver or reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: An authority may provide copies without charge or at a reduced charge where it determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.
rules.trigger: Authority determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest
rules.source_language: An authority may provide copies of a record without charge or at a reduced charge where the authority determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.
rules.notes: Discretionary waiver branch. There is no as-of-right indigency exemption from fees (George v. Record Custodian, 169 Wis. 2d 573).

rules.legal_concept: Fee cap for records produced by a contractor
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction/transcription incurred by the contractor
rules.atomic_rule: If a record is produced or collected by a non-authority under contract with an authority, the authorized fee for a copy may not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction or transcription incurred by that person, unless a fee is otherwise established by law.
rules.trigger: Record was produced/collected by a contractor of the authority
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding par. (a), if a record is produced or collected by a person who is not an authority pursuant to a contract entered into by that person with an authority, the authorized fees for obtaining a copy of the record may not exceed the actual, necessary, and direct cost of reproduction or transcription of the record incurred by the person who makes the reproduction or transcription, unless a fee is otherwise established or authorized to be established by law.
rules.notes: Records produced/collected under contract are accessible to the same extent as if maintained by the authority (19.36(3)).

rules.legal_concept: Law enforcement audio/video redaction fee
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio/video content
rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency may impose a fee for the actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is required by law, but may not charge if: the requester (an individual) certifies non-commercial use; the event is an officer-involved shooting; the requester has made 10 or fewer audio/video requests to that agency that calendar year; or the agency did not first provide a written fee estimate.
rules.trigger: Law enforcement agency redacts audio/video content in response to a request
rules.source_language: A law enforcement agency may impose a fee upon a requester for the actual, necessary, and direct cost of redacting recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is necessary to comply with applicable constitutional, statutory, or common law. [Fee prohibited where the requester certifies non-commercial use (false certification: $10,000 forfeiture per violation); where the event is an officer-involved shooting; where the requester has made 10 or fewer such requests that calendar year; or where the agency did not first provide a written fee estimate.]
rules.source_authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(am), created by 2023 Wis. Act 253
rules.effective_status: Effective per 2023 Wis. Act 253; requires manual verification of effective date and exact statutory text
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: the primary statute site (docs.legis.wisconsin.gov) and Justia were inaccessible; text assembled from official-source summaries and the Legislative Council act memo. VERIFY verbatim wording, subdivision structure, exact effective date, and the written-fee-estimate condition against the codified 19.35(3)(am). This is a narrow exception to the general no-redaction-fee rule (WI-0033).

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment of fees exceeding $5
rules.clock_spec: fixed: prepayment may be required when total fees exceed $5
rules.atomic_rule: An authority may require prepayment of any fee(s) imposed under sub. (3) if the total amount exceeds $5.
rules.trigger: Total fees imposed exceed $5
rules.source_language: An authority may require prepayment by a requester of any fee or fees imposed under this subsection if the total amount exceeds $5.
rules.notes: $5 is a fixed statutory threshold. Prepayment may not be demanded for amounts of $5 or less (Borzych v. Paluszcyk).

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment where prisoner owes prior fees
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester is a prisoner (or person confined in a federal institution in this state) who failed to pay a fee for a previous request, the authority may require prepayment of both the previously owed amount and the current amount.
rules.trigger: Prisoner-requester has an unpaid prior fee
rules.source_language: If the requester is a prisoner, as defined in s. 301.01 (2), or is a person confined in a federal correctional institution located in this state, and he or she has failed to pay any fee that was imposed by the authority for a request made previously by that requester, the authority may require prepayment both of the amount owed for the previous request and the amount owed for the current request.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment based on reasonable estimate
rules.atomic_rule: The amount of prepayment required for copies may be based on a reasonable estimate.
rules.trigger: Authority requires prepayment before copying
rules.source_language: The amount of prepayment required for copies may be based on a reasonable estimate.
rules.source_authority: State ex rel. Hill v. Zimmerman, 196 Wis. 2d 419, 538 N.W.2d 608 (Ct. App. 1995)

rules.legal_concept: Custodian's option on copy method for in-person requests
rules.atomic_rule: If a requester appears personally to request a copy of a copyable record, the authority may, at its option, permit the requester to copy the record or provide the requester with a copy substantially as readable as the original.
rules.trigger: Requester appears in person to request a copy
rules.source_language: If a requester appears personally to request a copy of a record that permits copying, the authority having custody of the record may, at its option, permit the requester to copy the record or provide the requester with a copy substantially as readable as the original.
rules.notes: The custodian, not the requester, chooses the copying method; the requester cannot insist on using their own equipment (Grebner v. Schiebel, 2001 WI App 17).

rules.legal_concept: Copy of audio recording or transcript
rules.atomic_rule: For a record that is a comprehensible audio recording, the requester has a right to a copy substantially as audible as the original; the authority may instead provide a transcript if the requester so requests.
rules.trigger: Requested record is a comprehensible audio recording
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, any requester has a right to receive from an authority having custody of a record which is in the form of a comprehensible audio recording a copy of the recording substantially as audible as the original. The authority may instead provide a transcript of the recording to the requester if he or she requests.

rules.legal_concept: Copy of video recording
rules.atomic_rule: For a record that is a video recording, the requester has a right to a copy substantially as good as the original.
rules.trigger: Requested record is a video recording
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, any requester has a right to receive from an authority having custody of a record which is in the form of a video recording a copy of the recording substantially as good as the original.

rules.legal_concept: Copy reduced to written form for non-comprehensible records
rules.atomic_rule: For a record not in a readily comprehensible form, the requester has a right to a copy of the information assembled and reduced to written form on paper.
rules.trigger: Requested record is not in readily comprehensible form
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, any requester has a right to receive from an authority having custody of a record which is not in a readily comprehensible form a copy of the information contained in the record assembled and reduced to written form on paper.
rules.notes: This is an express exception to the no-duty-to-create-a-record limit (WI-0050).

rules.legal_concept: Inspection/photograph of records whose form does not permit copying
rules.atomic_rule: For a record whose form does not permit copying, the requester has a right to inspect it; the authority may permit the requester to photograph it, and if the requester requests a photograph be provided, the authority shall provide a good quality photograph.
rules.trigger: Requested record's form does not permit copying
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding par. (b) and except as otherwise provided by law, any requester has a right to inspect any record not specified in pars. (c) to (e) the form of which does not permit copying. If a requester requests permission to photograph the record, the authority having custody of the record may permit the requester to photograph the record. If a requester requests that a photograph of the record be provided, the authority shall provide a good quality photograph of the record.
rules.notes: Photographing fee governed by WI-0036.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: Except as necessary to comply with pars. (c)-(e) or s. 19.36(6), the law does not require an authority to create a new record by extracting information from existing records and compiling it in a new format.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating a new record/compilation
rules.source_language: Except as necessary to comply with pars. (c) to (e) or s. 19.36 (6), this subsection does not require an authority to create a new record by extracting information from existing records and compiling the information in a new format.
rules.notes: Redacting thousands of documents under 19.36(6) does not amount to creating a new record (Osborn v. Board of Regents, 2002 WI 83). No obligation to provide direct access to an authority's electronic databases (WIREdata, 2008 WI 69).

rules.legal_concept: Exception for materials published for sale
rules.atomic_rule: The inspection/copy rights in pars. (a)-(c), (e) and (f) do not apply to a record that has been or will be promptly published with copies offered for sale or distribution.
rules.trigger: Record is/will be promptly published with copies offered for sale
rules.source_language: Paragraphs (a) to (c), (e) and (f) do not apply to a record which has been or will be promptly published with copies offered for sale or distribution.

rules.legal_concept: Restrictions on access to irreplaceable/fragile originals
rules.atomic_rule: A legal custodian may impose reasonable restrictions on the manner of access to an original record if the record is irreplaceable or easily damaged.
rules.trigger: Requested original record is irreplaceable or easily damaged
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding pars. (a), (am), (b) and (f), a legal custodian may impose reasonable restrictions on the manner of access to an original record if the record is irreplaceable or easily damaged.

rules.legal_concept: Compliance with legally prescribed access/use restrictions
rules.atomic_rule: A requester shall comply with any regulations or restrictions upon access to or use of information that are specifically prescribed by law.
rules.trigger: A specific statute prescribes restrictions on access/use of the record
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding pars. (a) to (f), a requester shall comply with any regulations or restrictions upon access to or use of information which are specifically prescribed by law.

rules.legal_concept: Destruction hold upon receipt of a request
rules.atomic_rule: No authority may destroy any record after receipt of a request for inspection or copying of that record until after the request is granted (or until the post-denial hold period expires).
rules.trigger: Authority receives a request for inspection/copying of the record
rules.source_language: No authority may destroy any record at any time after the receipt of a request for inspection or copying of the record under sub. (1) until after the request is granted or until at least 60 days after the date that the request is denied ...
rules.notes: Preservation-hold state triggered by the request itself (keeper sliver). Post-denial duration in WI-0055; litigation extension in WI-0056.

rules.legal_concept: 60/90-day post-denial destruction hold
rules.clock_spec: sets-deadline: 60 calendar-days from denial (90 calendar-days if requester is a committed or incarcerated person)
rules.atomic_rule: After a denial, the record may not be destroyed until at least 60 days after the denial date, or at least 90 days after the denial date if the requester is a committed or incarcerated person.
rules.trigger: Request is denied
rules.source_language: ... until after the request is granted or until at least 60 days after the date that the request is denied or, if the requester is a committed or incarcerated person, until at least 90 days after the date that the request is denied.
rules.notes: Fixed statutory durations. Day-counting per 19.345 (WI-0024).

rules.legal_concept: Destruction hold pending s. 19.37 action
rules.atomic_rule: If an authority receives written notice that a s. 19.37 action relating to a record has been commenced, the record may not be destroyed until the court's order and the appeal deadline have passed (or, if appealed, until the appellate order issues); if production is ordered and not appealed, not until the request is granted.
rules.trigger: Authority receives written notice of a commenced s. 19.37 action
rules.source_language: If an authority receives written notice that an action relating to a record has been commenced under s. 19.37, the record may not be destroyed until after the order of the court in relation to such record is issued and the deadline for appealing that order has passed, or, if appealed, until after the order of the court hearing the appeal is issued.
rules.notes: Litigation-triggered preservation hold (keeper sliver).

rules.legal_concept: Woznicki pre-release notice to record subject
rules.clock_spec: sets-deadline: within 3 days after the decision to permit access
rules.atomic_rule: If an authority decides to permit access to a specified record (employee disciplinary-investigation records, records obtained by subpoena/search warrant, or private-employer records about an employee), it shall, before permitting access and within 3 days after deciding to permit access, serve written notice on the record subject by certified mail or personal service, describing the record and the subject's rights under subs. (3) and (4).
rules.trigger: Authority decides to release a record within the three enumerated categories
rules.source_language: ... if an authority decides under s. 19.35 to permit access to a record specified in this paragraph, the authority shall, before permitting access and within 3 days after making the decision to permit access, serve written notice of that decision on any record subject to whom the record pertains, either by certified mail or by personally serving the notice on the record subject. The notice shall briefly describe the requested record and include a description of the rights of the record subject under subs. (3) and (4).
rules.notes: WI-specific 'Woznicki' notice path. Applies only to the three enumerated record categories (19.356(2)(a)1.-3.), with exceptions in pars. (b)-(d).

rules.legal_concept: Record subject's notice of intent to seek restraining order
rules.clock_spec: sets-deadline: within 5 days after receipt of the 19.356(2)(a) notice
rules.atomic_rule: Within 5 days after receipt of a notice under s. 19.356(2)(a), a record subject may provide written notification to the authority of intent to seek a court order restraining release.
rules.trigger: Record subject received a pre-release notice
rules.source_language: Within 5 days after receipt of a notice under sub. (2) (a), a record subject may provide written notification to the authority of his or her intent to seek a court order restraining the authority from providing access to the requested record.

rules.legal_concept: Record subject action to restrain release
rules.clock_spec: sets-deadline: within 10 days after receipt of the 19.356(2)(a) notice
rules.atomic_rule: Within 10 days after receipt of a notice under s. 19.356(2)(a), a record subject may commence an action naming the authority as defendant to restrain release; the requester may intervene as of right.
rules.trigger: Record subject received a pre-release notice
rules.source_language: Within 10 days after receipt of a notice under sub. (2) (a), a record subject may commence an action seeking a court order to restrain the authority from providing access to the requested record. If a record subject commences such an action, the record subject shall name the authority as a defendant. Notwithstanding s. 803.09, the requester may intervene in the action as a matter of right.
rules.notes: Judicial reverse-appeal by the record subject (namespaced appeal.judicial to distinguish from the requester's mandamus). The court shall issue a decision within 10 days after complete filings, and in any event within 30 days (19.356(7)).

rules.legal_concept: 12-day hold on release after notice
rules.clock_spec: sets-deadline: no release within 12 days of sending the 19.356(2)(a) notice; further hold during pendency of any action/appeal
rules.atomic_rule: An authority shall not provide access to a requested record within 12 days of sending a record-subject notice under s. 19.356(2)(a); if the record subject commences an action, the authority shall not release during the pendency of the action (and through any appeal/review period).
rules.trigger: A record-subject notice under 19.356(2)(a) has been sent
rules.source_language: An authority shall not provide access to a requested record within 12 days of sending a notice pertaining to that record under sub. (2) (a). In addition, if the record subject commences an action under sub. (4), the authority shall not provide access to the requested record during pendency of the action.
rules.notes: Mandatory release-hold; extends through appeal/petition-for-review periods per the remainder of sub. (5).

rules.legal_concept: Notice and augmentation for public-office record subjects
rules.clock_spec: sets-deadline: notice within 3 days of decision to permit access; record subject may augment within 5 days after receipt of notice
rules.atomic_rule: If an authority decides to permit access to a record relating to a record subject who is an officer/employee holding a local or state public office, it shall within 3 days serve written notice on the subject; the subject may within 5 days augment the record with written comments/documentation, and the authority shall release the record as augmented.
rules.trigger: Authority decides to release a record relating to a current public-office holder
rules.source_language: ... if an authority decides under s. 19.35 to permit access to a record containing information relating to a record subject who is an officer or employee of the authority holding a local public office or a state public office, the authority shall, before permitting access and within 3 days after making the decision to permit access, serve written notice ... Within 5 days after receipt of a notice under par. (a), a record subject may augment the record to be released with written comments and documentation selected by the record subject. ... the authority ... shall release the record as augmented by the record subject.
rules.notes: Applies only to current (not former) public-office holders, and only where the record 'relates to' that subject (OAG 7-14; OAG 2-18).

rules.legal_concept: Mandamus action by requester
rules.atomic_rule: If an authority withholds or delays access to a record after a written request, the requester may bring an action for mandamus asking a court to order release of the record.
rules.trigger: Authority withholds/delays a record after a written request
rules.source_language: If an authority withholds a record or a part of a record or delays granting access to a record or part of a record after a written request for disclosure is made, the requester may pursue either, or both, of the alternatives under pars. (a) and (b). (a) The requester may bring an action for mandamus asking a court to order release of the record.
rules.notes: Judicial review path (namespaced appeal.judicial). Notice-of-claim statutes ss. 893.80/893.82 do not apply (19.37(1n)).

rules.legal_concept: Application to attorney general or district attorney
rules.atomic_rule: As an alternative or additional path, the requester may request in writing that the district attorney of the county where the record is found, or the attorney general, bring a mandamus action; that official may bring such an action.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks review of a withholding/delay via AG or DA
rules.source_language: The requester may, in writing, request the district attorney of the county where the record is found, or request the attorney general, to bring an action for mandamus asking a court to order release of the record to the requester. The district attorney or attorney general may bring such an action.
rules.notes: Namespaced appeal.administrative (application to AG/DA) to distinguish from the requester's own judicial mandamus (WI-0062). The requester does not control an AG-brought action (State v. Zien, 2008 WI App 153).

rules.legal_concept: Written request required to enforce
rules.atomic_rule: A request must be in writing before an action to enforce the request is commenced under s. 19.37.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to commence an enforcement action
rules.source_language: A request may be made orally, but a request must be in writing before an action to enforce the request is commenced under s. 19.37.
rules.notes: Gates the enforcement path: only a written request (or written statement of an oral denial's reasons) supports mandamus.

rules.legal_concept: 90-day mandamus limit for committed/incarcerated persons
rules.clock_spec: sets-deadline: mandamus must be commenced within 90 days after the denial date (committed/incarcerated requesters only)
rules.atomic_rule: A committed or incarcerated person may not commence a mandamus action to challenge a denial later than 90 days after the date the request is denied.
rules.trigger: Committed/incarcerated requester's request is denied
rules.source_language: No action for mandamus under sub. (1) to challenge the denial of a request for access to a record or part of a record may be commenced by any committed or incarcerated person later than 90 days after the date that the request is denied by the authority having custody of the record or part of the record.
rules.notes: Applies only to committed/incarcerated persons; no analogous statutory limitation period is stated for other requesters.

rules.legal_concept: Applicant identity opt-out for public positions
rules.atomic_rule: An applicant for a position with an authority may indicate in writing that they do not wish their identity revealed; if so (and the applicant is not a final candidate or certified for a classified-service position), the authority shall not provide access to any record that may reveal the applicant's identity.
rules.trigger: Applicant submits a written non-disclosure indication and is not a final candidate
rules.source_language: Every applicant for a position with any authority may indicate in writing to the authority that the applicant does not wish the authority to reveal his or her identity. Except with respect to an applicant whose name is certified for appointment to a position in the state classified service or a final candidate, if an applicant makes such an indication in writing, the authority shall not provide access to any record related to the application that may reveal the identity of the applicant.
rules.notes: 'Final candidate' is defined in 19.36(7)(a); the five most qualified (or all, if fewer than five) applicants are final candidates whose identities are not shielded.

rules.legal_concept: 19.35(4)(c) determination sequence for self-access requests
rules.atomic_rule: When an identified individual (or authorized person) requests a record containing personally identifiable information about themselves, the authority shall first determine the right under sub. (1)(a); if a right exists it grants; if not, it then determines the right under sub. (1)(am) and grants or denies accordingly.
rules.trigger: Identified individual requests own PII under sub. (1)(a) or (am)
rules.source_language: If an authority receives a request under sub. (1) (a) or (am) from an individual or person authorized by the individual who identifies himself or herself and states that the purpose of the request is to inspect or copy a record containing personally identifiable information pertaining to the individual ..., the authority shall deny or grant the request in accordance with the following procedure: 1. The authority shall first determine if the requester has a right to inspect or copy the record under sub. (1) (a). 2. If [so], the authority shall grant the request. 3. If [not], the authority shall then determine if the requester has a right to inspect or copy the record under sub. (1) (am) and grant or deny the request accordingly.
rules.notes: A general public-records request does NOT trigger this sequence (Seifert v. School District of Sheboygan Falls, 2007 WI App 207).

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary withholding of trade secrets
rules.atomic_rule: An authority may withhold access to any record or portion of a record containing information qualifying as a trade secret as defined in s. 134.90(1)(c).
rules.trigger: Record contains trade-secret information
rules.source_language: An authority may withhold access to any record or portion of a record containing information qualifying as a trade secret as defined in s. 134.90 (1) (c).
rules.notes: Discretionary ('may withhold'); operationally supports partial withholding/redaction of the trade-secret portion.

material_negatives.note: Wisconsin sets NO fixed numeric response/acknowledgment deadline. The only time-for-compliance standard is the soft 'as soon as practicable and without delay' (19.35(4)(a); captured as rule WI-0023). There is no separate statutory acknowledgment-letter requirement and no day-count within which a determination must issue.

No commercial-purpose fee distinction or surcharge exists. Fees are limited to actual/necessary/direct cost regardless of purpose, and records may not be denied merely because the requester has a commercial purpose (58 Atty. Gen. 67). No 'commercial requester' branch to configure.

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate. The only constraint is the 'actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription' ceiling (19.35(3)(a), WI-0035); the city/authority supplies the operative per-unit value under that ceiling.

No fee is authorized for mere inspection. The four permitted fee tasks are reproduction/transcription, photographing/processing, locating (only if $50+), and mailing/shipping (19.35(3)); inspection itself carries no charge.

No statutory clarification clock or mandatory duty to help a requester narrow an overbroad request. A custodian need not take affirmative steps to limit a search and may (at some point) reject an insufficiently limited request (Gehl v. Connors; Schopper v. Gehring). Sufficiency is judged by the soft 'reasonably describes' standard (WI-0011).

No general statutory right to a record in a requester-specified electronic/native format or to direct access to an authority's databases; PDF satisfied an 'electronic/digital' request and requesters are not entitled to query databases directly (WIREdata v. Village of Sussex, 2008 WI 69). Format rights are limited to the medium-specific provisions in 19.35(1)(c)-(f).

No formal internal administrative-appeal tribunal or records ombudsman with binding authority. Review is via mandamus (court) or application to the AG/DA (19.37(1)); the AG may also give non-binding advisory interpretations under 19.39.
No deposit regime beyond the single prepayment rule (prepayment permitted when total fees exceed $5, 19.35(3)(f), WI-0042). No tiered deposit schedule or escrow requirement is specified.

structural_branches.description: Woznicki record-subject pre-release notice path (19.356(2)-(5)): 3-day notice to subject, subject's 5-day intent and 10-day restraint-action windows, and a 12-day (plus pendency) release hold. A WI-specific reverse-review branch the engine must execute before releasing the three enumerated record categories.

Public-office record-subject augmentation path (19.356(9)): 3-day notice then a 5-day window for the subject to augment the record with written comments/documentation, with mandatory release as augmented.

19.35(4)(c) ordered determination sequence for identified self-access requests: evaluate sub.(1)(a) first, grant if a right exists, otherwise evaluate sub.(1)(am). A distinct decision fork not present for general requests.

Request- and litigation-triggered destruction-hold states (19.35(5)): the record enters a preservation state on receipt of the request (until grant or 60/90-day post-denial period) and a further hold on written notice of a s. 19.37 action.

Local-IT-authority custodian passthrough (19.35(7)): a request to a local IT authority storing law-enforcement records is not answered by it; it must deny the local-law-enforcement portion and the owning authority is the custodian.

Two-track enforcement fork (19.37(1)): requester's own mandamus action (judicial) and/or written application to the AG or DA (administrative), each with distinct remedies; a written request is a prerequisite to either.

rules.legal_concept: Right of every person to inspect public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person (no requester qualification) has a right to inspect any public record of an Oregon public body, subject only to the stated exemptions.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of any person)
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to inspect any public record of a public body in this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by ORS 192.338, 192.345 and 192.355.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared eligibility key. 'Every person' establishes standing for any requester.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: Oregon imposes no residency requirement; the inspection right runs to every person regardless of residency.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to inspect any public record of a public body in this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by ORS 192.338, 192.345 and 192.355.
rules.notes: No residency limitation appears in the statute; 'every person' carries no residency qualifier. Emitted as rule with shared key so cross-state join matches states that state this as an absence.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose or reason to exercise the inspection right; no purpose is a condition of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to inspect any public record of a public body in this state, except as otherwise expressly provided by ORS 192.338, 192.345 and 192.355.
rules.notes: No statutory statement-of-purpose condition. Purpose may bear on fee-waiver 'public interest' analysis (OR-0023) but is not a precondition to the right. Emitted as rule with shared key.

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers copy/inspection duty
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian's duty to give a copy or a reasonable opportunity to inspect is triggered upon receipt of a written request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request by the custodian
rules.source_language: A public body that is the custodian of any public record that a person has a right to inspect shall give the person, upon receipt of a written request: (a) A copy of the public record if the public record is of a nature permitting copying; or (b) A reasonable opportunity to inspect or copy the public record.
rules.notes: Writing is the intake channel that triggers the copy obligation and the acknowledgment clock.

rules.legal_concept: Public body must publish a written request procedure
rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall make available to the public a written procedure for making public records requests that names one or more individuals (with addresses) to whom requests may be sent and states the amounts and manner of calculating fees.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation)
rules.source_language: A public body shall make available to the public a written procedure for making public records requests that includes: (a) The name of one or more individuals within the public body to whom public records requests may be sent, with addresses; and (b) The amounts of and the manner of calculating fees that the public body charges for responding to requests for public records.
rules.notes: Conjunctive requirement kept in one row; drives routing (designated recipient) and fee disclosure. The 5-business-day acknowledgment clock (OR-0006) runs from receipt by an individual identified in this procedure.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day acknowledgment of request
rules.atomic_rule: When an individual identified in the public body's written procedure receives a written request, the public body shall within five business days acknowledge receipt or complete its response.
rules.trigger: Receipt of written request by an individual identified in the public body's ORS 192.324(7) procedure
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of request by the designated individual
rules.source_language: If an individual who is identified in a public body's procedure described in subsection (7)(a) of this section receives a written request to inspect or receive a copy of a public record, the public body shall within five business days after receiving the request acknowledge receipt of the request or complete the public body's response to the request.
rules.notes: Acknowledgment clock; the 10-business-day statement deadline (OR-0008) counts from the date acknowledgment is due under this subsection.

rules.legal_concept: Required content of acknowledgment (custody determination)
rules.atomic_rule: The acknowledgment must confirm the public body is the custodian, inform the requester it is not the custodian, or notify the requester it is uncertain whether it is the custodian.
rules.trigger: Issuance of an acknowledgment under ORS 192.324(2)
rules.source_language: An acknowledgment under this subsection must: (a) Confirm that the public body is the custodian of the requested record; (b) Inform the requester that the public body is not the custodian of the requested record; or (c) Notify the requester that the public body is uncertain whether the public body is the custodian of the requested record.
rules.notes: Custody determination at acknowledgment drives routing (keeper-sliver: custodian/who-must-respond).

rules.legal_concept: Ten-business-day completion-or-status statement
rules.atomic_rule: As soon as reasonably possible but not later than 10 business days after the date acknowledgment is due, the public body shall either complete its response or provide a written statement that it is still processing plus a reasonable estimated completion date.
rules.trigger: Expiry of the date by which acknowledgment is required under ORS 192.324
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from the date acknowledgment is due under ORS 192.324(2)
rules.source_language: As soon as reasonably possible but not later than 10 business days after the date by which a public body is required to acknowledge receipt of the request under ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records), a public body shall: (a) Complete its response to the public records request; or (b) Provide a written statement that the public body is still processing the request and a reasonable estimated date by which the public body expects to complete its response based on the information currently available.
rules.notes: This is NOT a completion deadline; option (b) permits a status statement with a self-set estimated date. Subject to the impracticability exception (OR-0029).

rules.legal_concept: Complete response as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay
rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall complete its response to a written public records request as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written public records request by an individual identified in the ORS 192.324 procedure
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay" from receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: A public body shall complete its response to a written public records request that is received by an individual identified in the public body's procedure described in ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay.
rules.notes: Soft standard: there is NO fixed numeric outer deadline for completing a response in Oregon. Config Home structural per soft-deadline rule; no day-count invented.

rules.legal_concept: When a response is complete — access/copies element
rules.atomic_rule: A response is complete (as to access) when the public body provides access to or copies of all requested non-exempt records in its possession or custody, or explains where the records are already publicly available.
rules.trigger: Public body finishing its response
rules.source_language: A public body's response to a public records request is complete when the public body: (a) Provides access to or copies of all requested records within the possession or custody of the public body that the public body does not assert are exempt from public disclosure, or explains where the records are already publicly available;
rules.notes: Head element of the completeness definition; ties to possession/custody, not mere control. Other completeness elements are split into OR-0011..OR-0015.

rules.legal_concept: Assertion of exemptions with legal citation
rules.atomic_rule: To complete a response the public body must assert any exemptions it believes apply and, if citing ORS 192.355(8) or (9), identify the state or federal law relied upon.
rules.trigger: Public body withholding records as exempt
rules.source_language: Asserts any exemptions from disclosure that the public body believes apply to any requested records and, if the public body cites ORS 192.355 (Public records exempt from disclosure) (8) or (9), identifies the state or federal law that the public body relied on in asserting the exemptions;
rules.notes: Partial-denial content requirement; triggers the review-rights notice (OR-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Segregation of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both exempt and nonexempt material, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination.
rules.trigger: A record contains both exempt and nonexempt material
rules.source_language: If any public record contains material which is not exempt under ORS 192.345 (Public records conditionally exempt from disclosure) and 192.355 (Public records exempt from disclosure), as well as material which is exempt from disclosure, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination.
rules.notes: Segregability duty; ORS 192.329(2)(c) makes compliance with 192.338 part of a complete response. Attorney time spent segregating is fee-includable (OR-0021).

rules.legal_concept: Written statement when not the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: To the extent the public body is not the custodian of requested records, it must provide a written statement to that effect.
rules.trigger: Public body is not the custodian of some or all requested records
rules.source_language: To the extent that the public body is not the custodian of records that have been requested, provides a written statement to that effect;
rules.notes: Routing signal to requester; part of completeness. Complements custody determination in the acknowledgment (OR-0007).

rules.legal_concept: Statement where existence cannot be acknowledged
rules.atomic_rule: Where state or federal law prohibits acknowledging whether a record exists (or acknowledgment would forfeit federal benefits or impose a sanction), the public body must provide a written statement to that effect citing the law relied on, unless the statement itself would violate law.
rules.trigger: State/federal law bars acknowledging existence of a requested record
rules.source_language: To the extent that state or federal law prohibits the public body from acknowledging whether any requested record exists or that acknowledging whether a requested record exists would result in the loss of federal benefits or imposition of another sanction, provides a written statement to that effect, citing the state or federal law that the public body relies on, unless the written statement itself would violate state or federal law; and
rules.notes: Glomar-type response path; part of completeness definition.

rules.legal_concept: Notice of right to seek review of denial
rules.atomic_rule: If the public body asserts any exemption, its response must include a statement that the requester may seek review under ORS 192.401, 192.411, 192.415, 192.418, 192.422, 192.427 and 192.431.
rules.trigger: Public body asserts one or more exemptions
rules.source_language: If the public body asserts that one or more requested records are exempt from public disclosure, includes a statement that the requester may seek review of the public body's determination pursuant to ORS 192.401 (Records of health professional regulatory boards, Health Licensing Office), 192.411 (Petition to review denial of right to inspect state public record), 192.415 (Procedure to review denial of right to inspect other public records), 192.418 (Effect of failure of Attorney General, district attorney or elected official to take timely action on inspection petition), 192.422 (Petition form), 192.427 (Procedure to review denial by elected official of right to inspect public records) and 192.431 (Court authority in reviewing action denying right to inspect public records).
rules.notes: Denial-notice content requirement linking to the administrative and judicial review paths.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of custodian (functional)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Custodian' means the person described in ORS 7.110 for court records, or a public body mandated (directly or indirectly) to create, maintain, care for or control a public record; a public body that is not the custodian and lacks control is not required to search for/produce a record.
rules.trigger: Determining which body must respond
rules.source_language: 'Custodian' means: (a) The person described in ORS 7.110 for purposes of court records; or (b) A public body mandated, directly or indirectly, to create, maintain, care for or control a public record. 'Custodian' does not include a public body that has custody of a public record as an agent of another public body that is the custodian unless the public body is expressly required by law to hold that public record.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: definition the software branches on for routing/who-must-respond. Quote reconstructed from ORS 192.311(1); verify the agent-exclusion clause against the official PDF.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable opportunity to inspect during business hours
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall furnish proper and reasonable opportunities for inspection and examination during usual business hours and reasonable facilities for making memoranda/abstracts, and for electronic records shall furnish proper and reasonable opportunity to assure access.
rules.trigger: Person has occasion to examine the records
rules.source_language: The custodian of any public records, including public records maintained in machine readable or electronic form, unless otherwise expressly provided by statute, shall furnish proper and reasonable opportunities for inspection and examination of the records in the office of the custodian and reasonable facilities for making memoranda or abstracts therefrom, during the usual business hours, to all persons having occasion to make examination of them. If the public record is maintained in machine readable or electronic form, the custodian shall furnish proper and reasonable opportunity to assure access.
rules.notes: Inspection modality; 'usual business hours' bounds when inspection occurs.

rules.legal_concept: Format of electronic/machine-readable records
rules.atomic_rule: If a public record is maintained in machine readable or electronic form, the public body shall provide a copy in the form requested if available; if not available in the form requested, it shall make the record available in the form in which it maintains the record.
rules.trigger: Requested record is maintained in machine readable/electronic form
rules.source_language: If the public record is maintained in a machine readable or electronic form, the public body shall provide a copy of the public record in the form requested, if available. If the public record is not available in the form requested, the public body shall make the public record available in the form in which the public body maintains the public record.
rules.notes: Format-selection branch for electronic records.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian's protective rules
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may adopt reasonable rules necessary to protect the records and to prevent interference with the regular discharge of the custodian's duties.
rules.trigger: Custodian's discretion
rules.source_language: The custodian of the records may adopt reasonable rules necessary for the protection of the records and to prevent interference with the regular discharge of duties of the custodian.
rules.notes: Permits local rules governing manner of inspection; 'reasonable' is a soft limit, not a fixed value.

rules.legal_concept: Fees reasonably calculated to reimburse actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse it for its actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the records in organization or media to meet the request.
rules.trigger: Public body makes records available in response to a request
rules.source_language: The public body may establish fees reasonably calculated to reimburse the public body for the public body's actual cost of making public records available, including costs for summarizing, compiling or tailoring the public records, either in organization or media, to meet the request.
rules.notes: No statewide fixed per-page or per-hour rate; the ceiling is the soft 'actual cost / reasonably calculated' standard and the city supplies the operative rates.
