rules.legal_concept: Attorney review/redaction time in fees; exclusion of exemption-analysis time
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may include in the fee the cost of attorney time spent reviewing, redacting, or segregating records into exempt and nonexempt, but may NOT include attorney time spent determining the application of ORS 192.311 to 192.478.
rules.trigger: Attorney time expended on a request
rules.source_language: The public body may include in a fee established under paragraph (a) of this subsection the cost of time spent by an attorney for the public body in reviewing the public records, redacting material from the public records or segregating the public records into exempt and nonexempt records. The public body may not include in a fee established under paragraph (a) of this subsection the cost of time spent by an attorney for the public body in determining the application of the provisions of ORS 192.311 to 192.478.
rules.notes: Conjunctive permission+prohibition kept in one row (the includable/not-includable line is a single fee-component rule). Drives fee composition.

rules.legal_concept: $25 fee threshold requiring written estimate and confirmation
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not establish a fee greater than $25 unless it first provides the requester written notification of the estimated fee amount and the requester confirms that it wants the public body to proceed.
rules.trigger: Estimated fee exceeds $25
rules.source_language: The public body may not establish a fee greater than $25 under this section unless the public body first provides the requester with a written notification of the estimated amount of the fee and the requester confirms that the requester wants the public body to proceed with making the public record available.
rules.notes: $25 is the fixed trigger value; the estimate-and-confirm step is a structural gate that pairs with the fee-suspension clock (OR-0024). City cannot raise the $25 trigger.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver or reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may furnish copies without charge or at a substantially reduced fee if it determines the waiver or reduction is in the public interest because making the record available primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Custodian determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public record may furnish copies without charge or at a substantially reduced fee if the custodian determines that the waiver or reduction of fees is in the public interest because making the record available primarily benefits the general public.
rules.notes: Discretionary branch; denial of a waiver is separately reviewable (OR-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Response obligation suspended pending fee payment
rules.atomic_rule: If the public body has informed the requester of a permitted fee, its obligation to complete the response is suspended until the fee is paid, waived by the body, or ordered waived.
rules.trigger: Public body informs requester of a fee under ORS 192.324(4)
rules.clock_spec: completion obligation tolled from date requester is informed of fee until fee paid or waived
rules.source_language: If a public body has informed a requester of a fee permitted under ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) (4), the obligation of the public body to complete its response to the request is suspended until the requester has paid the fee, the fee has been waived by the public body pursuant to ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) (5) or the fee otherwise has been ordered waived.
rules.notes: Tolls the soft completion duty (OR-0009) while fee is outstanding.

rules.legal_concept: Close of request after 60 days' nonpayment
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester fails to pay the fee within 60 days of being informed of the fee (or within 60 days of denial of a fee waiver), the public body shall close the request.
rules.trigger: 60 days elapse after fee notice or waiver denial without payment
rules.clock_spec: 60 calendar-days from date requester informed of fee, or from date of fee-waiver denial; on lapse the request closes
rules.source_language: If the requester fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the fee, or fails to pay the fee within 60 days of the date on which the public body informed the requester of the denial of the fee waiver, the public body shall close the request.
rules.notes: Terminal event (request ends). 60-day count is fixed by statute.

rules.legal_concept: Petition to review unreasonable denial of fee waiver/reduction
rules.atomic_rule: A requester who believes there has been an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or reduction may petition the Attorney General or district attorney in the same manner as when inspection is denied, and the reviewer/court has the same authority.
rules.trigger: Requester believes a fee waiver/reduction was unreasonably denied
rules.source_language: A requester who believes that there has been an unreasonable denial of a fee waiver or fee reduction may petition the Attorney General or the district attorney in the same manner as a requester who petitions when inspection of a public record is denied under ORS 192.311 to 192.478. The Attorney General, the district attorney and the court have the same authority in instances when a fee waiver or reduction is denied as when inspection of a public record is denied.
rules.notes: Routes fee-waiver disputes into the same administrative-review path as denials.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith clarification request suspends response duty
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may request additional information or clarification to expedite its response; if made in good faith, its obligation to further complete the response is suspended until the requester provides the information/clarification or affirmatively declines.
rules.trigger: Public body makes a good-faith request for information or clarification
rules.clock_spec: further-completion obligation tolled from clarification request until requester responds or declines
rules.source_language: A public body may request additional information or clarification from a requester of public records for the purpose of expediting the public body's response to the request. If the public body has requested additional information or clarification in good faith, the public body's obligation to further complete its response to the request is suspended until the requester provides the requested information or clarification or affirmatively declines to provide that information or clarification.
rules.notes: Tolls the completion duty; paired with the 60-day close (OR-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Close of request after 60 days' failure to clarify
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester fails to respond within 60 days to a good-faith request for information or clarification, the public body shall close the request.
rules.trigger: 60 days elapse after a good-faith clarification request without requester response
rules.clock_spec: 60 calendar-days from the good-faith clarification request; on lapse the request closes
rules.source_language: If the requester fails to respond within 60 days to a good faith request from the public body for information or clarification, the public body shall close the request.
rules.notes: Terminal event; 60-day count fixed by statute.

rules.legal_concept: Impracticability suspension of statutory time periods
rules.atomic_rule: The ORS 192.324 and 192.329(5) time periods do not apply when compliance would be impracticable because necessary staff/volunteers are unavailable (including those on leave or not scheduled), compliance would demonstrably impede other necessary services, or because of the volume of simultaneous requests; the body must still respond as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay.
rules.trigger: Compliance with the acknowledgment/status deadlines would be impracticable for a listed reason
rules.clock_spec: numeric acknowledgment (5 bd) and status (10 bd) deadlines suspended for a listed impracticability reason; soft 'as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay' standard substitutes
rules.source_language: The time periods established by ORS 192.324 (Copies or inspection of public records) and subsection (5) of this section do not apply to a public body if compliance would be impracticable because: (a) The staff or volunteers necessary to complete a response to the public records request are unavailable; (b) Compliance would demonstrably impede the public body's ability to perform other necessary services; or (c) Of the volume of public records requests being simultaneously processed by the public body. ... A public body that cannot comply with the time periods established by ORS 192.324 and subsection (5) of this section for a reason listed in subsection (6) of this section shall, as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay, acknowledge a public records request and complete the response to the request.
rules.notes: Subsection (7) deems staff on leave/not scheduled to be 'unavailable' (kept in this row as it defines a term within the exception). Suspends the numeric deadlines and reverts to the soft standard.

rules.legal_concept: Petition to Attorney General to review state-agency denial
rules.atomic_rule: Any person denied inspection or a copy of a state-agency public record may petition the Attorney General to review whether the record may be withheld; the burden is on the agency to sustain its action.
rules.trigger: Denial of inspection/copy of a state agency public record
rules.source_language: Subject to ORS 192.401 (1) and 192.427, any person denied the right to inspect or to receive a copy of any public record of a state agency may petition the Attorney General to review the public record to determine if it may be withheld from public inspection. Except as provided in ORS 192.401 (2), the burden is on the agency to sustain its action.
rules.notes: Administrative-review path for STATE agencies (namespaced appeal.administrative). Local bodies use the DA path (OR-0032).

rules.legal_concept: AG must rule on petition within seven days
rules.atomic_rule: The Attorney General shall issue an order denying, granting, or partly denying and partly granting the petition within seven days from the day the AG receives the petition.
rules.trigger: AG receives a petition to review a denial
rules.clock_spec: 7 days from AG's receipt of the petition
rules.source_language: Except as provided in ORS 192.401 (2), the Attorney General shall issue an order denying or granting the petition, or denying it in part and granting it in part, within seven days from the day the Attorney General receives the petition.
rules.notes: Same 7-day deadline applies to the DA for local bodies via ORS 192.415(1). Failure to meet it is a deemed denial (OR-0033).

rules.legal_concept: District-attorney review for non-state public bodies
rules.atomic_rule: For a denial by a public body other than a state agency, the district attorney of the county where the body is located carries out the AG's review functions, and any suit must be filed in that county's circuit court.
rules.trigger: Denial by a public body other than a state agency (e.g., a municipality)
rules.source_language: ORS 192.401 and 192.411 apply to the case of a person denied the right to inspect or to receive a copy of any public record of a public body other than a state agency, except that: (a) The district attorney of the county in which the public body is located, or if it is located in more than one county the district attorney of the county in which the administrative offices of the public body are located, shall carry out the functions of the Attorney General; (b) Any suit filed must be filed in the circuit court for the county described in paragraph (a) of this subsection; and (c) The district attorney may not serve as counsel for the public body, in the cases permitted under ORS 192.411 (3), unless the district attorney ordinarily serves as counsel for the public body.
rules.notes: This is the path that governs MUNICIPAL denials. Routes review to the county DA rather than the AG.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial when AG/DA fails to rule in seven days
rules.atomic_rule: Failure of the AG or DA to issue an order on a petition within seven days of receipt is treated as an order denying the petition, enabling the requester to institute injunctive or declaratory relief proceedings.
rules.trigger: 7 days elapse after AG/DA receipt of petition without an order
rules.clock_spec: 7 days from receipt of petition; on lapse the petition is deemed denied
rules.source_language: The failure of the Attorney General or district attorney to issue an order under ORS 192.401, 192.411 or 192.415 denying, granting, or denying in part and granting in part a petition to require disclosure within seven days from the day of receipt of the petition shall be treated as an order denying the petition for the purpose of determining whether a person may institute proceedings for injunctive or declaratory relief under ORS 192.401, 192.411 or 192.415.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: deemed/constructive denial trigger (silence = denial). Remedy amounts excluded; the trigger is kept.

rules.legal_concept: Agency must comply with disclosure order within seven days or notice suit
rules.atomic_rule: If the AG orders disclosure, the state agency shall comply in full within seven days after issuance of the order unless within that period it issues a notice of intent to seek injunctive or declaratory relief; it must then institute the proceedings within seven days after issuing the notice.
rules.trigger: AG grants (or partly grants) petition and orders disclosure
rules.clock_spec: 7 days from issuance of AG order to comply or notice suit; then 7 days from notice to institute proceedings
rules.source_language: If the Attorney General grants the petition and orders the state agency to disclose the public record, or if the Attorney General grants the petition in part and orders the state agency to disclose a portion of the public record, the state agency shall comply with the order in full within seven days after issuance of the order, unless within the seven-day period it issues a notice of its intention to institute proceedings for injunctive or declaratory relief in the Circuit Court for Marion County or, as provided in ORS 192.401 (3), in the circuit court of the county where the public record is held. ... The state agency shall institute the proceedings within seven days after it issues its notice of intention to do so.
rules.notes: Post-order compliance/appeal clock for the public body. Applies to local bodies via the DA per ORS 192.415.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial when elected official fails to act in seven days
rules.atomic_rule: Failure of an elected official to grant or deny a request within seven days of receipt is treated as a denial, enabling the requester to institute injunctive or declaratory relief proceedings.
rules.trigger: 7 days elapse after an elected official's receipt of a request without action
rules.clock_spec: 7 days from elected official's receipt of the request; on lapse the request is deemed denied
rules.source_language: The failure of an elected official to deny, grant, or deny in part and grant in part a request to inspect or receive a copy of a public record within seven days from the day of receipt of the request shall be treated as a denial of the request for the purpose of determining whether a person may institute proceedings for injunctive or declaratory relief under ORS 192.401, 192.411 or 192.415.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: deemed-denial trigger specific to records held by elected officials. Distinct 7-day silence-equals-denial clock.

rules.legal_concept: Direct judicial review of elected-official denials
rules.atomic_rule: Where an elected official has custody of, or claims the right to withhold, a public record, no petition to the AG/DA may be filed (or considered after the official's withholding claim); the requester may instead institute injunctive or declaratory relief directly in circuit court.
rules.trigger: Elected official has custody of or claims right to withhold the requested record
rules.source_language: In any case in which a person is denied the right to inspect or to receive a copy of a public record in the custody of an elected official, or in the custody of any other person but as to which an elected official claims the right to withhold disclosure, no petition to require disclosure may be filed with the Attorney General or district attorney, or if a petition is filed it shall not be considered by the Attorney General or district attorney after a claim of right to withhold disclosure by an elected official. In such case a person denied the right to inspect or to receive a copy of a public record may institute proceedings for injunctive or declaratory relief in the appropriate circuit court...
rules.notes: Oregon-specific fork: elected-official records bypass the administrative-review stage and go straight to court (judicial namespace).

rules.legal_concept: Circuit court de novo review and production order
rules.atomic_rule: In a suit to compel disclosure the circuit court has jurisdiction to enjoin withholding and order production of records improperly withheld; it determines the matter de novo with the burden on the public body, may review documents in camera, and may punish noncompliance as contempt.
rules.source_language: In any suit filed under ORS 192.401, 192.411, 192.415, 192.422 or 192.427, the court has jurisdiction to enjoin the public body from withholding records and to order the production of any records improperly withheld from the person seeking disclosure. The court shall determine the matter de novo and the burden is on the public body to sustain its action. The court, on its own motion, may view the documents in controversy in camera before reaching a decision. Any noncompliance with the order of the court may be punished as contempt of court.
rules.notes: Judicial-review stage (namespaced appeal.judicial). Attorney-fee remedy in ORS 192.431(3) deliberately excluded per the Remove list.

rules.legal_concept: Expedited docket precedence for disclosure suits
rules.atomic_rule: Except for causes the court considers of greater importance, disclosure proceedings take precedence on the docket over all other causes and are assigned for hearing/trial at the earliest practicable date and expedited in every way.
rules.trigger: Proceedings arising under ORS 192.401, 192.411, 192.415, 192.422 or 192.427
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: hearing/trial at 'the earliest practicable date' and 'expedited in every way'
rules.source_language: Except as to causes the court considers of greater importance, proceedings arising under ORS 192.401, 192.411, 192.415, 192.422 or 192.427 take precedence on the docket over all other causes and shall be assigned for hearing and trial at the earliest practicable date and expedited in every way.
rules.notes: Soft scheduling standard within the judicial stage; Config Home structural per undefined-soft rule.

rules.legal_concept: Litigation-party request must also be served on public body's attorney
rules.atomic_rule: A requester who is a party to a civil judicial proceeding to which a public body is a party (or who filed an ORS 30.275(5)(a) tort-claim notice) and who requests a record known to relate to that proceeding must submit the request in writing to the custodian and, at the same time, to the attorney for the public body.
rules.trigger: Requester is a civil-litigation party/tort-claim-notice filer requesting a record known to relate to the proceeding
rules.source_language: If a person who is a party to a civil judicial proceeding to which a public body is a party, or who has filed a notice under ORS 30.275 (5)(a), asks to inspect or to receive a copy of a public record that the person knows relates to the proceeding or notice, the person must submit the request in writing to the custodian and, at the same time, to the attorney for the public body.
rules.notes: Special intake-routing branch for litigation-related requests; for a state agency the attorney is the Attorney General in Salem (ORS 192.314(2)(b)).

structural_branches.description: Each public body must publish a written request procedure naming designated recipient(s) with addresses and fee-calculation method (ORS 192.324(7)) — the intake/routing entry point.
Acknowledgment must make a custody determination (custodian / not custodian / uncertain), a three-way branch that drives routing (ORS 192.324(2)).
Oregon-specific suspension of the 5- and 10-business-day deadlines for staff unavailability, service impediment, or request volume, reverting to a soft standard (ORS 192.329(6)-(8)).
Municipal/non-state denials are reviewed by the county district attorney (not the AG), with suit in that county's circuit court (ORS 192.415).
Records held by, or withholding-claimed by, an elected official bypass administrative AG/DA review and go directly to circuit court (ORS 192.427) — a distinct Oregon path.
AG/DA silence for 7 days is a deemed denial that unlocks the judicial stage (ORS 192.418(1)).
Elected-official silence for 7 days is a deemed denial unlocking direct judicial relief (ORS 192.418(2)).
A stated fee tolls the completion obligation until paid/waived, feeding the 60-day nonpayment close (ORS 192.329(3)).
A good-faith clarification request tolls the completion obligation until the requester responds or declines, feeding the 60-day clarification close (ORS 192.329(4)).

material_negatives.note: Oregon sets NO fixed numeric outer deadline to complete a response. ORS 192.329(1) requires completion 'as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay' (soft), and the only hard 10-business-day duty (ORS 192.329(5)) is satisfied by a status statement with a self-set estimated date, not actual completion.

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate or per-hour labor rate. Fees are bounded only by the soft 'reasonably calculated to reimburse actual cost' standard (ORS 192.324(4)(a)); each city sets its own rates in its published procedure.

No express provision in ORS 192.311-192.478 imposing a litigation/appeal- or request-triggered preservation hold on records subject to a pending request. Routine retention schedules live in ORS ch. 192/166 archives provisions and are out of scope. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statute expressly authorizes or requires advance deposits/prepayment beyond the ORS 192.324(4)(c) $25 written-estimate-and-confirmation gate and the ORS 192.329(3) fee-payment suspension. Deposit practice, if any, is local.
No statutory requirement that a public body assign or provide a tracking number/reference for a request. Not legally required; excluded from primary rules.
Statute requires a written acknowledgment/response content but does not prescribe a delivery channel (mail/email/portal); channel is unspecified by statute.

rules.legal_concept: Public right of access to government data
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect and copy public government data upon request to the responsible authority or designee, at reasonable times and places.
rules.trigger: A person requests access to public government data.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data at reasonable times and places.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per the shared eligibility key. Access runs to 'a person' with no qualifier.

rules.legal_concept: Access without regard to requester's interest or purpose
rules.atomic_rule: The responsible authority must provide access to public data to any person without regard to the nature of that person's interest in the data; no statement of purpose may be required.
rules.trigger: A person requests public data.
rules.source_language: The responsible authority shall provide access to public data to any person, without regard to the nature of that person's interest in the data.
rules.notes: 'Without regard to the nature of that person's interest' also supports that a requester need not identify themselves for public data; identification-not-required is folded into this concept.

rules.legal_concept: No residency condition on access
rules.atomic_rule: Access to public government data is available to any person; the statute imposes no residency requirement.
rules.trigger: A person requests public government data.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data at reasonable times and places.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared key. No residency condition appears anywhere in Ch. 13; the 'a person' grant is unqualified as to residence.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to establish request-handling procedures
rules.atomic_rule: Each government entity's responsible authority must establish procedures to ensure requests for government data are received and complied with in an appropriate and prompt manner.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing duty).
rules.source_language: The responsible authority in every government entity shall establish procedures, consistent with this chapter, to insure that requests for government data are received and complied with in an appropriate and prompt manner.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt / reasonable-time response standard
rules.atomic_rule: The responsible authority must comply with a data request in an appropriate and prompt manner; a response must be provided within a reasonable time.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request for government data.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "appropriate and prompt manner" / "reasonable time" from request receipt
rules.source_language: The responsible authority in every government entity shall establish procedures, consistent with this chapter, to insure that requests for government data are received and complied with in an appropriate and prompt manner.
rules.source_authority: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 2; Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 3
rules.notes: Soft standard — no numeric statewide deadline for general public-data requests. Minn. R. 1205.0300, subp. 3 restates it as 'a response to a request for access within a reasonable time.' Do not convert to a day-count.

rules.legal_concept: Time to supply copies when not immediately available
rules.atomic_rule: If the responsible authority cannot provide copies at the time of request, copies must be supplied as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.trigger: Copies cannot be provided at the moment of request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as reasonably possible" from request
rules.source_language: If the responsible authority or designee is not able to provide copies at the time a request is made, copies shall be supplied as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.notes: Soft delivery standard; structural, not a city-filled numeric value.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for inspection of public data
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for inspection of public data; charges are authorized only when the requester asks for copies or electronic transmittal.
rules.trigger: A person inspects (rather than requests copies of) public data.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: $0 for inspection
rules.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time.
rules.notes: Charging authority is conditioned on a request for copies/electronic transmittal; inspection therefore carries no fee (negative implication of the quoted clause).

rules.legal_concept: Actual costs of searching for and retrieving data
rules.atomic_rule: When copies or electronic transmittal are requested, the responsible authority may require payment of the actual costs of searching for and retrieving the data, including employee time.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for copies or electronic transmittal.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost (search + retrieval + employee time)
rules.source_language: If a person requests copies or electronic transmittal of the data to the person, the responsible authority may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of searching for and retrieving government data, including the cost of employee time.
rules.notes: Constraint is 'actual costs' as a recovery ceiling; the city sets the operative rate/basis under it. Search/retrieval cost is NOT chargeable on the 100-or-fewer-page standard-copy path (see MN-0009).

rules.legal_concept: 25-cent-per-page cap for 100 or fewer standard pages
rules.atomic_rule: For requests of 100 or fewer black-and-white letter/legal-size paper copies, actual costs may not be used; the entity may charge no more than 25 cents per page copied.
rules.trigger: Request for 100 or fewer black-and-white, letter or legal size paper copies.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.25/page (≤100 pages, b/w letter/legal)
rules.source_language: If 100 or fewer pages of black and white, letter or legal size paper copies are requested, actual costs shall not be used, and instead, the responsible authority may charge no more than 25 cents for each page copied.
rules.notes: Ceiling of $0.25/page; city may charge less. Displaces the actual-cost basis on this small-request path.

rules.legal_concept: Cost of making and certifying copies for a data subject
rules.atomic_rule: When a data subject requests copies of data about themselves, the responsible authority may require payment of the actual costs of making and certifying the copies.
rules.trigger: Data subject requests copies of data about themselves.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of making and certifying copies
rules.source_language: The responsible authority or designee may require the requesting person to pay the actual costs of making and certifying the copies.
rules.notes: Data-subject copy path (own data). Distinct from the general public-data copy fee; note this covers copies only, inspection is free (MN-0011).

rules.legal_concept: Data subject shown own data without charge
rules.atomic_rule: A data subject who requests to see private or public data about themselves must be shown the data without any charge and, if desired, informed of its content and meaning.
rules.trigger: Data subject requests to be shown data about themselves.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: $0 to be shown own data
rules.source_language: Upon further request, an individual who is the subject of stored private or public data on individuals shall be shown the data without any charge and, if desired, shall be informed of the content and meaning of that data.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to provide copy in electronic form from computer storage
rules.atomic_rule: An entity maintaining public data in a computer storage medium must provide a copy in electronic form if it can reasonably make the copy or have it made.
rules.trigger: Request for public data that is maintained in a computer storage medium.
rules.source_language: The responsible authority of a government entity that maintains public government data in a computer storage medium shall provide to any person making a request under this section a copy of any public data contained in that medium, in electronic form, if the government entity can reasonably make the copy or have a copy made.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to convert to a different format or program
rules.atomic_rule: The entity is not required to provide data in an electronic format or program different from the one in which it maintains the data.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks data in a format/program other than the one maintained.
rules.source_language: This does not require a government entity to provide the data in an electronic format or program that is different from the format or program in which the data are maintained by the government entity.
rules.notes: Limits the electronic-copy duty in MN-0012.

rules.legal_concept: Presumption that all government data is public
rules.atomic_rule: All government data is public unless classified by statute, temporary classification, or federal law as not public (nonpublic/protected nonpublic, or, for data on individuals, private or confidential).
rules.trigger: Any request for government data.
rules.source_language: All government data collected, created, received, maintained or disseminated by a government entity shall be public unless classified by statute, or temporary classification pursuant to section 13.06, or federal law, as nonpublic or protected nonpublic, or with respect to data on individuals, as private or confidential.
rules.notes: Default-to-release presumption gating every request. Verify exact wording of the trailing classification list against the codified text on production.

rules.legal_concept: Classification fixed as of the time access is requested
rules.atomic_rule: The classification of data (and thus its accessibility) is determined by the law applicable to the data at the time the request for access is made.
rules.trigger: A request for access to data is made.
rules.source_language: The classification of data is determined by the law applicable to the data at the time a request for access to the data is made.
rules.notes: Clause text is verbatim; the subdivision citation within § 13.03 should be confirmed against the codified text before publication.

rules.legal_concept: Responsible authority or designee as the respondent
rules.atomic_rule: Requests are made to, and must be acted on by, the responsible authority or its designee.
rules.trigger: A person makes a data request.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data at reasonable times and places.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing (who must respond).

rules.legal_concept: Data practices compliance official
rules.atomic_rule: Each government entity must designate an employee to act as its data practices compliance official to handle questions and problems regarding access to data.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing designation duty).
rules.source_language: Each government entity shall designate an employee of the government entity to act as the entity's data practices compliance official to handle questions regarding data access problems. (paraphrase pending verbatim confirmation)
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver routing role (escalation point for access problems). Source fetched but returned as a fragment/summary; confirm verbatim wording on production.

rules.legal_concept: Denial notice with citation to the classifying authority
rules.atomic_rule: If the responsible authority denies access because data is classified, it must inform the requester of the determination orally at the time of the request or in writing as soon after as possible, and cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or federal-law provision on which the determination is based.
rules.trigger: Responsible authority determines requested data is classified so as to deny access.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "in writing as soon after that time as possible" from the request
rules.source_language: If the responsible authority or designee determines that the requested data is classified so as to deny the requesting person access, the responsible authority or designee shall inform the requesting person of the determination either orally at the time of the request, or in writing as soon after that time as possible, and shall cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or specific provision of federal law on which the determination is based.
rules.notes: Soft written-notice deadline; structural. Written form may be oral first, then written.

rules.legal_concept: Written certification of denial upon requester's request
rules.atomic_rule: Upon the request of any person denied access, the responsible authority must certify in writing that the request was denied and cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or federal-law provision on which the denial was based.
rules.trigger: A denied requester asks for written certification.
rules.source_language: Upon the request of any person denied access to data, the responsible authority or designee shall certify in writing that the request has been denied and cite the specific statutory section, temporary classification, or specific provision of federal law upon which the denial was based.
rules.notes: Written certification is triggered by the requester's ask, on top of the automatic denial notice in MN-0018.

rules.legal_concept: Ten-day response to a data subject's access request
rules.atomic_rule: For a data subject's request about their own data, the responsible authority must comply immediately if possible, or within ten days of the request excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays if immediate compliance is not possible.
rules.trigger: An individual requests data about themselves under § 13.04, subd. 3.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 10 days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from date of request
rules.source_language: The responsible authority or designee shall comply immediately, if possible, with any request made pursuant to this subdivision, or within ten days of the date of the request, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, if immediate compliance is not possible.
rules.notes: Hard numeric deadline, but scoped to data-subject requests for their OWN data — not general public-data requests (which carry only the soft standard in MN-0005). 'Ten days ... excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays' = business days; ceiling because 'immediately if possible' can be sooner.

rules.legal_concept: Informing individual whether they are a data subject and the classification
rules.atomic_rule: Upon request, an individual must be informed whether they are the subject of stored data on individuals and whether that data is classified as public, private, or confidential.
rules.trigger: An individual asks whether they are the subject of stored data.
rules.source_language: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, an individual shall be informed whether the individual is the subject of stored data on individuals, and whether it is classified as public, private or confidential.

rules.legal_concept: Data subject shown data and informed of its content and meaning
rules.atomic_rule: Upon further request, a data subject must be shown their private or public data and, if desired, informed of its content and meaning.
rules.trigger: Data subject makes a further request to see the data.
rules.source_language: Upon further request, an individual who is the subject of stored private or public data on individuals shall be shown the data without any charge and, if desired, shall be informed of the content and meaning of that data.
rules.notes: Same sentence also grounds the free-inspection fee rule MN-0011; this row captures the show-and-explain duty.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day response to a data-accuracy challenge
rules.atomic_rule: Upon a data subject's challenge to accuracy or completeness, the responsible authority must within 30 days either correct the data or notify the individual that it has determined the data to be correct.
rules.trigger: Data subject contests the accuracy or completeness of public or private data about themselves.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 30 days from receipt of the data subject's notification
rules.source_language: Upon receiving notification from the data subject, the responsible authority shall within 30 days either: (1) correct the data found to be inaccurate or incomplete and attempt to notify past recipients of inaccurate or incomplete data, including recipients named by the individual; or (2) notify the individual that the responsible authority believes the data to be correct.
rules.notes: Verbatim reconstructed from opened source; option (1)/(2) wording (esp. the past-recipient notice and 'believes the data to be correct') should be confirmed against codified text on production.

rules.legal_concept: 60-day appeal of accuracy determination to the commissioner
rules.atomic_rule: A data subject may appeal an accuracy determination to the commissioner, and must submit the appeal within 60 days of the responsible authority's notice of the right to appeal.
rules.trigger: Responsible authority issues an accuracy determination with notice of the right to appeal.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 60 days from the responsible authority's notice of the right to appeal
rules.source_language: An individual must submit an appeal to the commissioner within 60 days of the responsible authority's notice of the right to appeal.
rules.notes: Administrative appeal path for the data-accuracy sub-workflow (distinct from access denials).

rules.legal_concept: Commissioner of Administration advisory opinion
rules.atomic_rule: A government entity, or any person who disagrees with a determination regarding data practices, may request a written advisory opinion from the Commissioner of Administration.
rules.trigger: A person disagrees with a data-practices determination (or an entity seeks guidance).
rules.source_language: any person who disagrees with a determination regarding data practices [may request an opinion from the commissioner]
rules.notes: Non-binding administrative review path. Quoted fragment is verbatim; bracketed operative verb reconstructed — confirm full sentence on production.

rules.legal_concept: 50-day deadline for commissioner to issue an opinion
rules.atomic_rule: The commissioner must issue an advisory opinion within 50 days of receipt of the request, unless notice of non-issuance is provided within five business days.
rules.trigger: Commissioner receives a valid advisory-opinion request.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 50 days from receipt of request (non-issuance notice within 5 business days)
rules.source_language: the commissioner shall issue an opinion within 50 days of receipt of the request
rules.notes: The 50-day clock runs on the commissioner (state actor), not the municipality. Five-business-day non-issuance notice is a related sub-clock; confirm its exact wording on production.

rules.legal_concept: OAH complaint to compel compliance
rules.atomic_rule: A complaint alleging a chapter-13 violation, for which an order to compel compliance is requested, may be filed with the Office of Administrative Hearings.
rules.trigger: A person alleges a data-practices violation and seeks an order to compel compliance.
rules.source_language: A complaint alleging a violation of this chapter for which an order to compel compliance is requested may be filed with the office.
rules.notes: Minnesota-specific administrative-enforcement path before the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH).

rules.legal_concept: Two-year deadline to file an OAH complaint
rules.atomic_rule: An OAH complaint must be filed within two years after the act or failure to act, or within one year after discovery where concealment or misrepresentation prevented earlier discovery.
rules.trigger: The act or failure to act that is the subject of the complaint occurs.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 2 years from the act/failure (or 1 year from discovery of concealment/misrepresentation)
rules.source_language: The complaint must be filed with the office within two years after the occurrence of the act or failure to act that is the subject of the complaint, except that if the act or failure to act involves concealment or misrepresentation by the government entity that could not be discovered during that period, the complaint may be filed with the office within one year after the concealment or misrepresentation is discovered.

rules.legal_concept: $1,000 OAH complaint filing fee
rules.atomic_rule: An OAH complaint must be accompanied by a $1,000 filing fee or a bond guaranteeing payment of the fee.
rules.trigger: Filing an OAH complaint.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: $1,000 filing fee (or bond)
rules.source_language: The complaint must be accompanied by a filing fee of $1,000 or a bond to guarantee the payment of this fee.
rules.notes: Filing fee gates the administrative-remedy path; fixed statutory amount (not a records-copy fee).

rules.legal_concept: 20-business-day probable-cause review by ALJ
rules.atomic_rule: An administrative law judge must conduct a probable-cause review of the OAH complaint within 20 business days.
rules.trigger: OAH complaint is filed.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 20 business days from filing (probable-cause review)
rules.source_language: Administrative law judge conducts probable cause review within 20 business days. (paraphrase pending verbatim confirmation)
rules.notes: Source opened but returned as a summary; confirm verbatim wording and exact trigger event on production.

rules.legal_concept: 30-business-day hearing after probable cause
rules.atomic_rule: If probable cause is found, a hearing must be held within 30 business days.
rules.trigger: Administrative law judge finds probable cause.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 30 business days from a probable-cause finding
rules.source_language: Hearing held within 30 business days if probable cause found. (paraphrase pending verbatim confirmation)
rules.notes: Source opened but returned as a summary; confirm verbatim wording on production.

rules.legal_concept: 10-business-day decision after hearing
rules.atomic_rule: The administrative law judge must issue a decision within 10 business days after the hearing record closes.
rules.trigger: The OAH hearing closes.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 10 business days after the hearing closes
rules.source_language: Judge issues decision within 10 business days after hearing closes. (paraphrase pending verbatim confirmation)
rules.notes: Source opened but returned as a summary; confirm verbatim wording on production.

rules.legal_concept: District court action to compel compliance
rules.atomic_rule: Any aggrieved person seeking to enforce their rights or obtain access to data may bring an action in district court to compel compliance with the chapter.
rules.trigger: A person is aggrieved by a data-practices violation or denial of access.
rules.source_language: any aggrieved person seeking to enforce the person's rights under this chapter or obtain access to data may bring an action in district court to compel compliance with this chapter
rules.notes: Judicial path — namespaced appeal.judicial.* separate from the administrative OAH/advisory-opinion paths. Damages/attorney-fee remedies in § 13.08 are excluded per the inclusion test.

rules.legal_concept: District court injunction against violations
rules.atomic_rule: A responsible authority or government entity that violates or proposes to violate the chapter may be enjoined by the district court.
rules.trigger: A violation or proposed violation of chapter 13.
rules.source_language: A responsible authority or government entity which violates or proposes to violate this chapter may be enjoined by the district court.
rules.notes: Injunctive judicial remedy; kept as a request-outcome path, not a damages remedy.

rules.legal_concept: Right to examine records; any person of the age of majority
rules.atomic_rule: Any person of the age of majority may inspect, copy, or reproduce any public record, except as otherwise provided by this Chapter or specifically provided by law.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right)
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter or as otherwise specifically provided by law, and in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, any person of the age of majority may inspect, copy, or reproduce any public record.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared eligibility key. Constitutional foundation: La. Const. art. XII, § 3. Age-of-majority applies to INSPECTION; see LA-0002 for copies.

rules.legal_concept: Right to obtain a copy or reproduction (no age limit)
rules.atomic_rule: Any person (no age-of-majority limit) may obtain a copy or reproduction of any public record.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter or as otherwise specifically provided by law, and in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, any person may obtain a copy or reproduction of any public record.
rules.notes: Distinguished from LA-0001: the age-of-majority condition attaches to in-person inspection, not to obtaining copies.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose; custodian may inquire only as to age and identification
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall make no inquiry of a requester except as to age and identification; no statement of purpose may be required.
rules.trigger: Person applies for a public record
rules.source_language: The custodian shall make no inquiry of any person who applies for a public record, except an inquiry as to the age and identification of the person and may require the person to sign a register and shall not review, examine, or scrutinize any copy, photograph, or memoranda in the possession of any such person.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared eligibility key.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to exercise the right of access
rules.atomic_rule: Access is available to any person of the age of majority; no Louisiana residency is required to inspect, copy, or reproduce a public record.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter or as otherwise specifically provided by law, and in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, any person of the age of majority may inspect, copy, or reproduce any public record.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per shared eligibility key. The 'no residency requirement' characterization is derived from the verbatim 'any person' clause; the statute imposes no residency condition. (Indigent-fee waiver in LA-0025 is separately limited to 'indigent citizens of this state.')

rules.legal_concept: Exclusion of certain post-conviction incarcerated individuals from 'person'
rules.atomic_rule: An individual in custody after sentence following a felony conviction who has exhausted appellate remedies is not a 'person' entitled to records unless the request is limited to grounds for post-conviction relief under C.Cr.P. art. 930.3.
rules.trigger: Requester is post-conviction, post-appeal incarcerated individual AND request not limited to post-conviction-relief grounds
rules.source_language: 'Person' does not include an individual in custody after sentence following a felony conviction who has exhausted his appellate remedies when the request for public records is not limited to grounds upon which the individual could file for post-conviction relief under Code of Criminal Procedure Article 930.3.
rules.notes: Eligibility branch: routes an otherwise-valid request out unless the record scope is limited to PCR grounds.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'public body' including municipal government
rules.atomic_rule: A 'public body' subject to the law includes any instrumentality of municipal government, its committees, and designated public/quasi-public nonprofit corporations.
rules.trigger: Body is an instrumentality of state/parish/municipal government
rules.source_language: the phrase "public body" means any branch, department, office, agency, board, commission, district, governing authority, political subdivision, or any committee, subcommittee, advisory board, or task force thereof, any other instrumentality of state, parish, or municipal government, including a public or quasi-public nonprofit corporation designated as an entity to perform a governmental or proprietary function, or an affiliate of a housing authority.
rules.notes: Establishes municipal coverage. Text confirmed present in current (2024) code.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'public records' and the security-feature exclusion
rules.atomic_rule: Documentary material used/possessed/retained in the conduct of public business is a 'public record' except as otherwise provided; security features of electronic/IT/security systems are not public records.
rules.trigger: Material used, in use, or retained for public business
rules.source_language: All books, records, writings, accounts, letters and letter books, maps, drawings, photographs, cards, tapes, recordings, memoranda, and papers, and all copies, duplicates, photographs, including microfilm, or other reproductions thereof ... having been used, being in use, or prepared, possessed, or retained for use in the conduct, transaction, or performance of any business, transaction, work, duty, or function which was conducted, transacted, or performed by or under the authority of the constitution or laws of this state ... are "public records", except as otherwise provided in this Chapter or the Constitution of Louisiana. ... Notwithstanding Subparagraph (a), any documentary material of a security feature of a public body's electronic data processing system, information technology system, telecommunications network, or electronic security system ... is not a "public record".
rules.notes: The definition the engine branches on to classify whether a request targets a public record. Verbatim from official-content compilation, re-confirmed against 2024 code; verify any later amendments.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'custodian'
rules.atomic_rule: The 'custodian' who must respond is the public official or head of the public body having custody or control of the record, or a representative specifically authorized by him to respond to inspection requests.
rules.trigger: Body has custody or control of the record
rules.source_language: the word "custodian" means the public official or head of any public body having custody or control of a public record, or a representative specifically authorized by him to respond to requests to inspect any such public records.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing / who-must-respond.

rules.legal_concept: Burden of proving non-disclosability rests with custodian
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian bears the burden of proving that a record is not subject to inspection, copying, or reproduction.
rules.trigger: Custodian withholds or disputes disclosability
rules.source_language: The burden of proving that a public record is not subject to inspection, copying, or reproduction shall rest with the custodian.
rules.notes: Presumption of openness; governs denial posture.

rules.legal_concept: Providing access is a duty of the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: Providing access to public records is a mandatory responsibility and duty of the custodian's office and its employees.
rules.trigger: Office holds public records
rules.source_language: Providing access to public records is a responsibility and duty of the appointive or elective office of a custodian and his employees.

rules.legal_concept: Request may be made in person, in writing, or electronically
rules.atomic_rule: A public-records request may be submitted in person, in writing, or electronically.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: the passage of five days, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays, from the date of his in-person, written, or electronic request without receiving a determination in writing by the custodian
rules.notes: Statute recognizes in-person, written, and electronic request channels (the request-method enum). No writing is required to inspect.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may verify identity and require signing a register
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may inquire as to the requester's age and identification and may require the requester to sign a register.
rules.trigger: Person applies to examine a record
rules.source_language: The custodian shall make no inquiry of any person who applies for a public record, except an inquiry as to the age and identification of the person and may require the person to sign a register
rules.notes: Bounded intake permission; pairs with LA-0003 (no other inquiry).

rules.legal_concept: Examination during regular office/working hours
rules.atomic_rule: Examination of records must occur during regular office or working hours unless the custodian authorizes examination at other times.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to examine records on site
rules.source_language: examinations of records under the authority of this Section must be conducted during regular office or working hours, unless the custodian shall authorize examination of records in other than regular office or working hours.
rules.notes: After-hours examination triggers overtime compensation (LA-0027).

rules.legal_concept: No fee to examine or review records
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged to examine or review a public record, or to determine whether a record is subject to disclosure, except as provided in this Section.
rules.trigger: Requester examines/reviews rather than copies
rules.source_language: No fee shall be charged to any person to examine or review any public records, except as provided in this Section, and no fee shall be charged for examination or review to determine if a record is subject to disclosure, except as may be determined by a court of competent jurisdiction.
rules.notes: Examination fee fixed at zero; copy fees governed separately (LA-0021).

rules.legal_concept: Immediate presentation when record not in active use
rules.atomic_rule: If the requested record is immediately available (not in active use), it shall be immediately presented to the requester.
rules.trigger: Record applied for is immediately available / not in active use
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "immediately" from application (when record not in active use)
rules.source_language: If the public record applied for is immediately available, because of its not being in active use at the time of the application, the public record shall be immediately presented to the authorized person applying for it.
rules.notes: 'Immediately' treated as an undefined-soft standard (config_home structural); no numeric day-count invented.

rules.legal_concept: Fix a day/hour within three days when record in active use
rules.atomic_rule: If the record is in active use, the custodian shall promptly certify this in writing and fix a day and hour within three days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) for the requester to exercise the right.
rules.trigger: Record applied for is in active use at time of application
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: within 3 business-days from application (excl. Sat/Sun/legal holidays)
rules.source_language: If the public record applied for is not immediately available, because of its being in active use at the time of the application, the custodian shall promptly certify this in writing to the applicant, and in his certificate shall fix a day and hour within three days, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays, for the exercise of the right granted by this Chapter.
rules.notes: This 3-business-day window is distinct from the 5-business-day 44:32(D) determination window (LA-0028) and the 5-day deemed-denial trigger (LA-0030).

rules.legal_concept: Duty to segregate records for reasonable public viewing
rules.atomic_rule: The responsible official shall segregate the requested record from other records so the public can reasonably view it; if segregation is unreasonably burdensome/expensive or unnecessary, the official shall so state in writing and state the record's location.
rules.trigger: Request made for a record to which the public is entitled
rules.source_language: When a request is made for a public record to which the public is entitled, the official ... who has responsibility for the record shall have the record segregated from other records under his custody so that the public can reasonably view the record. If, however, segregating the record would be unreasonably burdensome or expensive, or if the record requested is maintained in a fashion that makes it readily identifiable and renders further segregation unnecessary, the official shall so state in writing and shall state the location of the requested record.
rules.notes: Search/identification duty (physical segregation for viewing), distinct from redaction of exempt content.

rules.legal_concept: Written certification when record not in custodian's custody/control
rules.atomic_rule: If the requested record is not in the custody/control of the person applied to, that person shall promptly certify in writing the reason for its absence, its location, who has custody, and how/when it left his custody.
rules.trigger: Requested record not in the custody or control of the person applied to
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from application
rules.source_language: If any public record applied for by any authorized person is not in the custody or control of the person to whom the application is made, such person shall promptly certify this in writing to the applicant, and shall in the certificate state in detail to the best of his knowledge and belief, the reason for the absence of the record from his custody or control, its location, what person then has custody of the record and the manner and method in which, and the exact time at which it was taken from his custody or control.
rules.notes: Routing branch: redirects requester toward the correct custodian. 'Promptly' is undefined-soft.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to provide copies
rules.atomic_rule: For non-state-agency public records, the custodian has a duty to provide copies to a requester, unless the requester fails to pay applicable copying fees after advance notice of the amount or has an outstanding balance from a prior request.
rules.trigger: Requester requests copies
rules.source_language: For all public records, except public records of state agencies, it shall be the duty of the custodian of the public records to provide copies to persons so requesting, unless the requestor fails to pay the applicable copying fees after being notified of the amount in advance of production or the requestor has an outstanding balance from a prior request.
rules.notes: Municipal/local scope. State-agency copy duty is the parallel 44:32(C)(2)(a).

rules.legal_concept: Electronic copies / transmission permitted
rules.atomic_rule: Copies provided may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
rules.trigger: Custodian provides copies
rules.source_language: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, which may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
rules.notes: Electronic transmission is permitted and feeable; the statute does not mandate a particular format or a format-preference regime.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee for making copies
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records.
rules.trigger: Requester requests copies
rules.source_language: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, which may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
rules.notes: Soft-standard: the state supplies only a 'reasonable' constraint; the municipality sets the operative per-page/per-item value. No statutory numeric cap for local bodies.

rules.legal_concept: Establish and post a reasonable fee schedule
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian who elects to collect copying fees shall establish a reasonable fee schedule and post it where it can be readily accessed by the public.
rules.trigger: Custodian elects to establish and collect copy fees
rules.source_language: Any custodian who elects to establish and collect such fees shall establish a reasonable fee schedule and post the schedule where it can be readily accessed by the public.
rules.notes: Conditional structural requirement triggered by electing to charge.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may request payment in advance of production
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may request payment of fees in advance of production.
rules.trigger: Fees apply to the request
rules.source_language: The custodian may request payment of fees in advance of production.

rules.legal_concept: Copies may be withheld for nonpayment or outstanding balance
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian need not provide copies where the requester fails to pay applicable copying fees after advance notice of the amount, or has an outstanding balance from a prior request.
rules.trigger: Requester fails to pay after advance notice OR has an outstanding prior balance
rules.source_language: it shall be the duty of the custodian of the public records to provide copies to persons so requesting, unless the requestor fails to pay the applicable copying fees after being notified of the amount in advance of production or the requestor has an outstanding balance from a prior request.
rules.notes: Production gate; branches the request to a hold-for-payment state.

rules.legal_concept: Waiver or reduction for indigent citizens
rules.atomic_rule: Copies of records may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge to indigent citizens of the state.
rules.trigger: Requester is an indigent citizen of Louisiana
rules.source_language: Copies of records may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge to indigent citizens of this state.
rules.notes: Discretionary waiver; limited to indigent 'citizens of this state.'

rules.legal_concept: State-agency copies charged per uniform schedule adopted by commissioner of administration
rules.atomic_rule: For state-agency public records, copy fees shall be charged according to the uniform fee schedule adopted by the commissioner of administration (R.S. 39:241) or as otherwise fixed by law.
rules.trigger: Request is to a state agency
rules.source_language: Fees for such copies shall be charged according to the uniform fee schedule adopted by the commissioner of administration as provided by R.S. 39:241 or as otherwise fixed or provided by law.
rules.notes: Agency-specific: applies to STATE agencies, NOT municipalities (which use the reasonable-fee standard, LA-0021). Included for cross-state overlap with 'statewide fee schedule set by a central agency' concept.

rules.legal_concept: Overtime compensation for after-hours examination
rules.atomic_rule: When examination is conducted outside regular working hours, persons representing the custodian are entitled to reasonable compensation, paid by the public body and funded in advance by the party demanding the extraordinary examination.
rules.trigger: Examination authorized outside regular office/working hours
rules.source_language: Custodian's representatives who supervise examination in other than regular working hours shall be entitled to reasonable compensation to be paid to them by the public body having custody of such record, out of funds provided in advance by the person examining such record in other than regular working hours.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: subsection B was summarized by the fetch tool, not opened verbatim; confirm exact wording. 'Reasonable compensation' is a soft-standard the city fills in.

rules.legal_concept: Five-day written determination when public-record status is questioned
rules.atomic_rule: When the custodian raises a question whether an item is a public record, the custodian shall, within five days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) of receipt of the request, notify the requester in writing of the determination and the reasons.
rules.trigger: Custodian raises a question whether the requested item is a public record
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: within 5 business-days from receipt of the written request (excl. Sat/Sun/legal holidays)
rules.source_language: In any case in which a record is requested and a question is raised by the custodian of the record as to whether it is a public record, such custodian shall within five days, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays, of the receipt of the request, in writing for such record, notify in writing the person making such request of his determination and the reasons therefor.
rules.notes: CURRENCY: this window is FIVE business days in current law (older sources say 'three days' — outdated for 44:32(D)). Conditional on the custodian questioning status; not a universal acknowledgment deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Denial notice must cite the legal basis for exemption
rules.atomic_rule: A written determination withholding a record (or part) must reference the basis under law the custodian determined exempts the record, or any part thereof, from inspection, copying, or reproduction.
rules.trigger: Custodian determines a record or part is exempt
rules.source_language: Such written notification shall contain a reference to the basis under law which the custodian has determined exempts a record, or any part thereof, from inspection, copying, or reproduction.
rules.notes: Notice-content requirement; the 'or any part thereof' phrasing is the statute's nearest hook for partial exemption/redaction, but no explicit segregate-and-release-the-remainder mandate exists.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive (deemed) denial after five days of nonresponse
rules.atomic_rule: Passage of five days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) from an in-person, written, or electronic request without receiving a written determination or a time estimate constitutes a denial, entitling the requester to enforcement proceedings.
rules.trigger: Five business days elapse from request with no written determination and no time estimate
rules.clock_spec: terminal: 5 business-days from request (in-person/written/electronic), excl. Sat/Sun/legal holidays, with no determination or estimate
rules.source_language: Any person who has been denied the right to inspect, copy, reproduce, or obtain a copy or reproduction of a record under the provisions of this Chapter, either by a determination of the custodian or by the passage of five days, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays, from the date of his in-person, written, or electronic request without receiving a determination in writing by the custodian or an estimate of the time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review of a records request, may institute proceedings for the issuance of a writ of mandamus, injunctive or declaratory relief
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver deemed-denial trigger (remedy amounts dropped). This is the closest thing to a universal response deadline: respond (or give a time estimate) within 5 business days or the request is constructively denied.

rules.legal_concept: Time estimate forestalls constructive denial
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may respond within the five-day window with an estimate of the time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review, which forestalls the constructive denial.
rules.trigger: Custodian cannot produce/determine within five days but responds with a time estimate
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review" from the estimate
rules.source_language: without receiving a determination in writing by the custodian or an estimate of the time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review of a records request
rules.notes: Structural alternative response path: providing a reasonable-time estimate prevents the deemed denial in LA-0030. The estimate itself is an undefined-soft standard.

rules.legal_concept: Judicial enforcement by writ of mandamus / injunctive / declaratory relief
rules.atomic_rule: A denied requester may institute proceedings for a writ of mandamus, injunctive or declaratory relief, together with attorney fees, costs and damages, in the district court for the parish where the custodian's office is located.
rules.trigger: Denial (actual or constructive) of the right of access
rules.source_language: may institute proceedings for the issuance of a writ of mandamus, injunctive or declaratory relief, together with attorney fees, costs and damages as provided for by this Section, in the district court for the parish in which the office of the custodian is located.
rules.notes: Judicial-appeal path (namespaced appeal.judicial.*). Louisiana provides NO administrative-appeal stage; the district court is the first review forum. Venue = parish of the custodian's office.

rules.legal_concept: Public-records suits tried by preference and summarily
rules.atomic_rule: A suit to enforce the Public Records Law shall be tried by preference and in a summary manner; appellate courts shall place it on the preferential docket and hear it without delay.
rules.trigger: Enforcement suit filed under the Chapter
rules.source_language: any suit brought in any court of original jurisdiction to enforce the provisions of this Chapter shall be tried by preference and in a summary manner, and any appellate courts to which the suit is brought shall place it on its preferential docket and shall hear it without delay.
rules.notes: Procedural acceleration attached to the judicial path.

rules.legal_concept: Denial when request would substantially disrupt government operations (after attempt to narrow)
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian reasonably determines a request would substantially disrupt required government operations, the custodian may deny access, but only after reasonable attempts to narrow or specify the request with the requester.
rules.trigger: Custodian reasonably determines the request would substantially disrupt required government operations
rules.source_language: If the custodian reasonably determines that the request would substantially disrupt required government operations, the custodian may deny access only after reasonable attempts to narrow or specify the request with the requestor.
rules.notes: Discretionary denial gated by a mandatory clarification/narrowing step; embeds the clarification.narrow_request concept. No clock on the narrowing dialogue.

material_negatives.note: No fixed universal acknowledgment deadline for ordinary requests. The 5-business-day 44:32(D) window applies only when the custodian QUESTIONS whether an item is a public record; the general obligation is functionally enforced by the 5-business-day constructive-denial trigger (44:35(A), LA-0030). Absence of a found universal-acknowledgment statute is not proof none exists.

No administrative-appeal stage exists in the Public Records Law. There is no AG/ombudsman/records-authority binding review; the Attorney General issues only advisory opinions. Enforcement is by direct suit in district court (44:35). Emitted as a negative so the cross-state join does not manufacture a phantom administrative stage.

No request- or litigation-triggered preservation/hold provision in the PRL. La. R.S. 44:36 imposes only a routine default 3-year retention (excluded as routine retention). No statute directs a custodian to freeze destruction because a request, appeal, or suit is pending.

No statewide statutory per-page or per-item copy-fee CAP for municipal/local custodians; the only constraint is 'reasonable' (44:32(C)(1)(a), LA-0021). A uniform dollar schedule exists only for STATE agencies (44:32(C)(2)(a), LA-0026).
No deadline governs the clarification/narrowing dialogue. The narrowing step under 44:32(A)(2) (LA-0034) is mandatory before a disruption-based denial but carries no statutory clock.

No statutory right to receive records in a requester-specified format. The custodian must provide copies and MAY transmit electronic copies (44:32(C)(1)(a), LA-0020), but no format-preference or native-format mandate is stated.
No statutory requirement to assign or communicate a tracking/reference number, or to maintain a public request log.

No absolute outer deadline for completing production of a voluminous request; the statute relies on the 'time reasonably necessary for collection, segregation, redaction, examination, or review' estimate (44:35(A), LA-0031) rather than a fixed maximum.

structural_branches.description: 44:33(B) forks on record availability: immediately-available records are presented immediately (LA-0015); records in active use route to a written certificate fixing a day/hour within 3 business days (LA-0016).
44:34 branch: when the record is not in the applied-to person's custody/control, the request routes to a written certification identifying reason, location, and the correct custodian (LA-0018).
44:32(D) branch: when the custodian questions public-record status, the request enters a 5-business-day written-determination-with-legal-basis state (LA-0028/LA-0029).
44:35(A) terminal branch: 5 business days without a written determination or a time estimate moves the request into a constructive-denial state that unlocks judicial enforcement (LA-0030).
44:35(A) alternative branch: issuing a reasonable-time estimate diverts the request off the constructive-denial track into an extended-processing state (LA-0031).
44:32(A)(2) branch: a request deemed to substantially disrupt operations must pass through a mandatory narrow/specify dialogue before a discretionary denial (LA-0034).
44:35 judicial path (no administrative predicate): district-court mandamus/injunctive/declaratory action, venued in the custodian's parish and tried by preference/summarily (LA-0032/LA-0033).

44:32(C)(1)(a) branch: nonpayment after advance notice, or an outstanding prior balance, holds production pending payment (LA-0023/LA-0024); after-hours examination routes to an overtime-compensation-prepaid path (LA-0027).

Research date: 2026-07-22. Most recent legislative session reviewed: 2024 Regular Session (statutes verified current via legis.la.gov as of July 2026; codified statutes were available and opened/quoted directly).

CURRENT-LAW STATEMENT: Louisiana's Public Records Law is codified at La. R.S. 44:1 et seq. (Title 44, Chapter 1), grounded in La. Const. art. XII, § 3. The operative request-processing sections (44:1, 44:31, 44:31.1, 44:32, 44:33, 44:34, 44:35) were opened and quoted verbatim from the official Louisiana State Legislature site (legis.la.gov). IMPORTANT CURRENCY NOTE: the custodian "questioned-record" written-determination window under 44:32(D) is FIVE business days in current law; older compilations/handbooks stating "three days" for 44:32(D) are outdated. The separate 3-business-day window survives only in 44:33(B) (fixing a day/hour when a record is in active use). The 44:1 definitions were read from a 2016 official-content compilation and re-confirmed against the 2024 code (public-body, custodian, and security-feature-exclusion language all present); manual re-verification of any post-2024 amendments recommended.

COVERAGE MATRIX: eligibility=Researched-rules-found; municipal coverage=rules-found; intake/submission=rules-found; scope & clarification=Partial (narrowing under 44:32(A)(2), no clock); classification=rules-found (44:32(D) status determination); deadlines & time calc=rules-found; search/identification=Partial (segregation duty; no numeric search-time standard beyond a "reasonably necessary" estimate); custody/routing=rules-found (44:34); communications/notices=rules-found; production/inspection=rules-found; electronic records/format=Partial (transmission permitted; no format-preference mandate); fees=rules-found; payment/deposits=rules-found; redaction/segregability=Partial (44:32(D) "any part thereof"; no explicit segregate-and-release mandate); denials=rules-found; administrative/AG review=Researched-none-found (AG opinions advisory only); appeals=rules-found (judicial only); enforcement trigger=rules-found (deemed denial); request tracking=none-found; special record types=selective (below).

EXCLUDED (with reason): La. R.S. 44:36 preservation/3-year default retention (routine records-retention schedule, NOT request-triggered — no request/litigation hold exists in the PRL); La. R.S. 44:35(E) actual damages and civil penalty not-to-exceed $100/day (remedy amounts — the response-duty trigger is kept via the deemed-denial rule); La. R.S. 44:35(D) attorney-fee award (attorney-fee provision on Remove list); bulk of La. R.S. 44:2–44:29 and the 44:4/44:4.1 incorporated exemption catalog (confidentiality lists — only those altering processing noted as special records); La. R.S. 44:9 criminal-record expungement procedure (record-specific court process, not general request handling); 44:4.1(A) legislative findings (policy statement).

SPECIAL RECORD TYPES (selective — create a distinct workflow/notice/review; flagged for human legal review): (1) Proprietary/trade-secret records (44:3.2) — custodian must immediately notify the developer/owner of the request before disclosure and make a determination within the 44:32(D)/44:33(B) time period; cover-sheet marking regime. (2) Law-enforcement / pending-criminal-litigation records (44:3) — separate withholding standard; the initial arrest/incident report remains public with enumerated fields. (3) Personnel records (44:11) — home address/phone (if requested confidential), SSN, and financial-institution direct-deposit info are confidential, triggering a redaction workflow. (4) Security features / interior building plans of public schools (44:1(A)(2)(b)) — not "public records." These require human legal review before automation.
